picks.headline: No. 13 Texas Tech vs. No. 22 Arizona Football Game Preview and Prediction
picks.blurb: No. 13 Texas Tech vs. No. 22 Arizona Football Game Preview and Prediction Skip to main content SI.COM Texas Tech Athletics Texas Tech hosts Arizona in this big time Big 12 showdown. The Texas Tech Red Raiders need to focus on boosting their offense for this one. Quarterback Will Hammond has 1,561 passing yards, but he has thrown only six touchdowns and has six interceptions on the season. Explosive running back J'Koby Williams has 619 rushing yards and 5 TDs, but if you take away the Arizona State and Oregon State games, he has been inconsistent for the Red Raiders this season. Kenny Johnson , a receiver, is the main downfield target but only has one touchdown reception this season and, besides the Houston and Arizona State games, has not had a significant impact on the Texas Tech passing attack. All three as well as some other key offensive players need to step up and have big games against Arizona to win this game. The defense has to get back to focusing and dominating like they have for a lot of the season. The Red Raiders have one of the most ball-hawking secondary units in the country, sitting near the top of NCAA FBS with 13 interceptions. Defensive lineman A.J. Holmes Jr. anchors the front seven and has 6 sacks this season. However, the Red Raiders are coming off their first loss of the season, a 37-24 loss to Cincinnati where they gave up 427 yards and gave up four passing touchdowns. They will be seeking to bounce back at home to stay undefeated at home this season. Arizona, on the other hand, has a five-game winning streak and defeated Cincinnati by a final score of 34-7. Their only loss of the season was to BYU on the road. Veteran quarterback Noah Fifita leads the Arizona Wildcats, who again have a high-efficiency passing offense, with Fifiti already having 2,064 passing yards and 18 TDs through seven games. Kedrick Reescano leads the ground game with just over 300 rushing yards and five touchdowns, while wideout Isaiah Mizell is an explosive playmaker with 493 yards and 5 TDs this season, most of which have come in the Wildcats' last two games against Iowa State and West Virginia. Linebacker Taye Brown has a team-leading 27 tackles and leads the Wildcats defense. Edge rusher Chase Kennedy leads the team in pressure rate with 4 sacks, and the Texas Tech offensive line has a tough task trying to stop him from getting to the quarterback. Arizona has a scoring defense that gives up only 16.7 points per game, but they did give up 31 points against West Virginia. Arizona recently crushed Iowa State 39-3 and has put up a total of just over 200 points in their last five games. The Wildcats are also 2-1 on the road this season heading into Lubbock for this top 25 game. The key matchup for this game will be Noah Fifita vs. the Texas Tech secondary. Fifita’s efficient throwing (almost 74% completion rate) will face immediate tests from a Red Raider defense that excels at creating takeaways via interceptions. Another major matchup in this game pits the Red Raiders offensive line against Arizona’s front seven on defense. Texas Tech’s running offense behind J’Koby Williams and Quinten Joyner will face a challenge against an Arizona front seven that is holding opponents under 110 rushing yards per game. This game also has Big 12 Championship ramifications since both teams are deadlocked at 3-1 in conference play behind undefeated Utah, and the winner is squarely in the race for a Big 12 Championship Game berth. An early game prediction for this game that may change slightly as the injury reports for both teams come out later this week, but the Red Raiders bounce back and win a very close game by a final score of Texas Tech 28, Arizona 27. There's a monster Big 12 matchup on Halloween as Arizona heads to Texas Tech for a game between two 6-1 squads that will inevitably shake up the standings. My Arizona vs. Texas Tech prediction questions Will Hammond's quality, and the best of my college football picks takes a look at a total of 54.5 that might be too high. This game will be broadcast on ESPN at 12 p.m. ET on Saturday, Oct. 31. TOP PICK Who will win Arizona vs Texas Tech: Arizona +3.5 Play Arizona at anything +3 or above. Texas Tech has a quarterback problem. Will Hammond has 13 turnover-worthy passes to pair with only eight big-time throws (per PFF), and his limitations have resulted in the third least-explosive passing attack in the nation . That makes them one-dimensional offensively, and it plays into Arizona's run-stopping defense. The Red Raiders don't block well enough up front (118th in front seven havoc allowed) to compensate for the quarterback deficiency. Tech's secondary has been hit for 266.1 passing yards per game, so the Wildcats (10th in passing success rate) will be able to chuck it around. Arizona vs Texas Tech Over/Under pick: Under 54.5 Tech's offensive limitations will show through in this matchup. Arizona's defense (14th in EPA per play, 11th in success rate) is much better than the market is accounting for, as it doesn't have name recognition but is well-coordinated under Danny Gonzales. On the flip side, Tech's defense checks in at 16th in EPA per play allowed and 10th in PFF's team defense grade. The strength of this team still resides on that side of the ball, and Joey McGuire will attempt to lean on that unit and minimize possessions for Fifita. Arizona's top three wide receivers have all been out. Tre Spivey is done for the year, while Giovanni Richardson and Chris Hunter III are considered questionable. The Wildcats can still move the ball in the air, but the efficiency won't be at its peak given the cluster injuries. Arizona vs Texas Tech combo Arizona got off to slow starts against Washington State and Northern Illinois, and could do so again during a difficult trip to Lubbock. Texas Tech has cashed the First Half Under in eight of its last 13 games. Given Hammond's turnover-prone ways and overall offensive issues, the defense should be the focal point over the second half of the season. Pete Fiutak Tue, October 27, 2026 at 11:28 PM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Texas Tech was cruising right along, looking like the star of the Big 12 again after a 53-25 blowout over Arizona State, and then it walked into a wall at Cincinnati, losing with a 37-24 thud. Arizona has been fantastic ever since its 28-17 loss at BYU early in the season, including a 34-7 win over Cincinnati. But it still has a few nasty games to go in November. Both teams are 6-1. The winner will be set up nicely for a College Football Playoff spot if it doesn't win the Big 12 title. The loser will still be alive for the CFP if it wins out, but getting to the Big 12 Championship in a loaded conference season will be tough. Arizona vs Texas Tech: Quick Hits Texas Tech still has to go to Oklahoma State, but it doesn't have to face BYU or Utah, and the other three games against West Virginia, at Baylor, and TCU aren't bad. Arizona gets three of its final four games at home, getting TCU and Utah next before going to Kansas State and finishing up against Arizona State. Texas Tech won the most recent matchup 28-22 in 2024 and is 5-2-1 in the series going back to 1975. How To Watch Arizona vs Texas Tech Arizona at Texas Tech Date: Saturday, October 31, 2026 Game Time: 12:00 PM ET TV: ESPN Location: Galaxy Stadium, Lubbock, TX – Week 9 Schedule, Game Previews – CFN Top 25 | Bowl Projections – Predicting the First CFP Top 25 – CFN Week 9 Expert Picks Why Arizona Will Win For the second time all year, Texas Tech played someone who could run well, and Cincinnati went off in the 13-point win. Houston can run. It ran 37 times for 175 yards against the Red Raiders, and lost when it couldn't hit a late two-point conversion. Cincinnati wasn't exactly more physical, but it found space on the way to a 255-yard day with big run after big run. Arizona's running game isn't a killer, but it's more than effective enough, working hand-in-hand with super-accurate quarterback Noah Fifita and an offense that's great at keeping the chains moving. Why Texas Tech Will Win Arizona doesn't take the ball away enough, and that matters in a huge way here. The Wildcats forced two takeaways in the win over Washington State, and two more in the win over West Virginia. That's about it, coming up with six on the year. Texas Tech has a huge problem with turnovers, with three against Cincinnati, two against Houston, and ten in the last five games. Don't turn it over, or at least stay even in the mistake battle, and the Red Raiders should be fine. Texas Tech has a great balance to its attack, and it needs to mix it up. BYU and West Virginia – in very different ways – both showed it's possible to move the ball efficiently against the Wildcat defense. Arizona vs Texas Tech Prediction, Betting Lines Is Arizona ready to show that it's really and truly a player, or will Texas Tech wipe away the Cincinnati loss like it was just a blip? It'll be a little of both, as Arizona controls the clock and tempo for the first half, but Texas Tech gets the pass rush working early in the second half. It'll be rough for the Red Raiders without pressuring Fifita, and they won't do enough of it over the final ten minutes. Score prediction for Arizona game Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Things have taken quite the turn for the Texas Tech football team after suffering its first loss of the season. Getting bested by Cincinnati for 60 minutes has put the Red Raiders in a pressure point. There's little wiggle room left for Joey McGuire's team to keep its hopes of repeating as Big 12 Conference champions alive. Now they have a talented Arizona team coming to Galaxy Stadium looking to kick the Red Raiders while they're down. What will it take for Texas Tech to walk away with the win? Is Arizona actually the favorite in this game? Our breakdown of the game, plus a score prediction. What's holding Texas Tech football back? It's a layered conversation as to what is keeping the Red Raiders from reaching their potential. For starters, the offense, led by quarterback Will Hammond, hasn't put up the kind of numbers Tech fans want. Receivers have struggled to get open (besides Kenny Johnson) and when they do create separation from their defenders, Hammond hasn't found them or delivered solid throws enough to take advantage. While the rushing game has been a point of scorn for some fans, J'Koby Williams has been electric, and Cameron Dickey is on track to rejoin him in the backfield this week. Defensively, the pass defense has been sporadic. The 13 interceptions (second in the nation) and five pick-6s count, but when those haven't come, opponents have had little trouble moving the ball through the air against the Red Raiders. These things have been present all year but only came to a head against Cincinnati. Now they face an Arizona team equipped to exploit these very issues. TEMPE, ARIZONA - NOVEMBER 25: Quarterback Noah Fifita #11 of the Arizona Wildcats walks out to the field before the NCAAF game against the Arizona State Sun Devils at Mountain America Stadium on November 25, 2023 in Tempe, Arizona. (Photo by Christian Petersen/Getty Images) What Arizona football can do to beat Texas Tech football The Wildcats rank sixth in the nation in total sacks (24.0), bringing constant pressure to opposing quarterbacks to get them out of rhythm. Cincinnati generated a season-high four sacks against the Red Raiders last week, while Arizona has three games with five or more sacks. Noah Fifita and the Arizona offense have also been operating at a high level, generating at least 280 yards through the air in six of the team's seven games. Fifita ranks third in the Big 12 with 2,064 passing yards, totaling 18 touchdowns to just four interceptions. The Wildcats have been hit with injuries to their receiving room, having already lost Tre Spivey for the season and seeing two others on the team's first availability report for the game. Even so, Arizona's offense has operated at a high level. Texas Tech football's notable streak on the line The Red Raiders have won their last 12 home games, which ranks one shy of the program record set during World War II when the Red Raiders won 13 straight games from 1939 to 1942. Score prediction for Texas Tech football vs. Arizona Arizona 35, Texas Tech 21: This is a pivot point for the Red Raiders to determine where they'll be in the Big 12 title race. Problem is, Texas Tech struggled to generate offense against a bad Cincinnati defense, and Arizona's defense has been quality all season. Bad recipe. picks.headline: Texas Tech-Arizona football predictions: Who wins key Big 12 game?
picks.blurb: Life comes at you fast. BYU and Texas Tech are licking their wounds after road losses to unranked teams and the league's commissioner Brett Yormark is headed out the door . The Red Raiders ' loss at Cincinnati stirred up a hornet's nest after Texas Tech billionaire booster Cody Campbell took to social media , saying: "There is no excuse or reason to lose a game like this. We have to be better." He stayed on social media throughout the week, dispelling any notion Tech coach Joey McGuire was under any sort of heat : "Joey McGuire is a perfect fit for our program, everybody, with an opinion that matters, loves him. He isn’t going anywhere." While the Red Raiders were feeling the burn of defeat, Wildcats fans were enjoying the burn of tequila. Arizona coach Brent Brennan ran up a $2,000 bar tab buying tequila shots for fans after the Wildcats' 39-3 homecoming win over Iowa State last Saturday. "I think it's important that if you want people to show up for you, you've got to show up for them and it was just an easy way for me to pop in there with all of our alumni in town and everybody for Homecoming and the excitement of the game to just go in there and say hello and get out," Brennan said. "I was there for five minutes and it was an expensive five minutes, but it was good five minutes." Just trying to invest in our fans and just let them know how much we appreciate them as a football team." Texas Tech (6-1, 3-1) fell from No. 5 in the US LBM Coaches poll to No. 14, while the Wildcats (6-1, 3-1) enter the Coaches Poll at No. 21 after five straight wins. Saturday's game has the potential to be a Big 12 championship game eliminator. So who wins? Here's what you need to know for one of Week 9's marquee games , including predictions from USA TODAY Sports reporters and beat writers from the Lubbock Avalanche-Journal , Arizona Republic and Arizona Daily Star , part of the USA TODAY Network. Texas Tech spent big in the offseason and expected Brendan Sorsby to lead its offense this year. But Sorsby's gambling addiction and subsequent drama that came with it, forced the Red Raiders to lean on Will Hammond under center. The junior hasn't been great this season, with the same amount of touchdowns as interceptions (six). Florida State transfer Thomas Castellanos was brought in as a backup option, and has played sparingly, but he "will receive an uptick in snaps" on Saturday, per ESPN's Pete Thamel . Castellanos has 6,494 career passing yards over stops at UCF, Boston College, FSU and now Texas Tech. Texas Tech expert previews the Arizona football game, makes a score prediction
picks.blurb: Texas Tech expert previews the Arizona Wildcats football game, makes a score prediction | Arizona Desert Swarm Skip to main content SB Nation SB Nation logo An Arizona Wildcats Community Arizona Desert Swarm October 31, 2026 Arizona Desert Swarm Notifications Notifications The Feed Sections Arizona Basketball Arizona Football Arizona Softball Arizona Recruiting Arizona Soccer Arizona Volleyball Arizona Baseball Arizona Gymnastics Arizona in the Pros Betting Betting News FanDuel College Football Odds FanDuel College Basketball Odds Arizona Football Odds Arizona Basketball Odds College Football Picks and Predictions College Basketball Picks and Predictions Login / Sign Up Search The Feed Sections Expand Arizona Basketball Betting Expand Betting News Community Guidelines All communities Notifications Arizona Football College football has one of the longest offseasons of any sport, which lends itself to certain players and teams generating a lot of hype and attention. Texas Tech falls squarely in that category, as its seemingly unlimited resources thanks to billionaire booster Cody Campbell made it a go-to place for top transfers out of the portal. But that also led to the ill-fated acquisition of quarterback Brendan Sorsby , who after leaving Cincinnati for Tech was revealed to have bet on college sports. Sorsby was banned by the NCAA, later reinstated, but the backlash led to him leaving the program before ever playing a game. Despite that, Tech was unbeaten before losing last week, dropping to No. 13 in the AP poll and into a tie for second place in the Big 12 with, among other teams, Arizona. That in effect makes Saturday’s matchup an unofficial elimination game for the conference title race. To better understand the Red Raiders, we reached out to Seth Jungman of Staking the Plains for some insight and a score prediction. Below are his eloquent answers to our inarticulate questions: AZ Desert Swarm: Outside of the irony of the first loss coming to Cincinnati, what were the biggest contributors to Texas Tech falling from the ranks of the unbeatens? Seth Jungman: “It’s the thing that I think Texas Tech fans have known, but maybe the national media wasn’t paying attention. I think most fans have known that the offense simply wasn’t very good and the defense isn’t as good as it was last year. Will Hammond is fine, but there’s a reason why the staff went out to get Brendan Sorsby before the season. They knew he probably wasn’t ready, but things happened and here we are. Also, I think it’s incredibly evident that the players who were part of this defense last year were truly special, particularly Jacob Rodriguez, David Bailey, and Romello Height. Getting to the quarterback to wreck offenses was the cheat code last year and this year, that’s simply not happening.” It’s fair to say that Will Hammond was not the first choice to lead this offense. How do you think he has performed to this point? What are his best attributes and where does he lack most? “I thought last week against Arizona State he took a step forward, but against Cincinnati he took two steps back. His best attributes is that he is a natural leader and he wants the ball in his hands and he wants to be the guy. My biggest problem with him is that I think he makes bad game management decisions. Knowing that the team needs points, he’ll heave the ball towards the end zone with a low chance of completion rather than take the play that keeps the drive alive. His lack of understanding of knowing when to take chances and when to churn yards is what bothers me the most.” What is the likelihood that Cameron Dickey will be back for this game? How would that impact the run game and the way J’Koby Williams, who has run for 680 yards and five touchdowns, get used? “I think chances are very good that he returns. It’s been about four weeks from the dreaded high-ankle sprain and that’s about the time. I don’t think it was a bad sprain so this game would seem about right and he was out doing some drills this past week. What Dickey offers is a guy that’s going to bruise and batter the opposing defense while Williams will break a 40-yard run in what looks like a lost play. Quinten Joyner has tried to fill that roll for Dickey, but it’s not the same. Joyner is coming off of ACL surgery and he doesn’t have the same burst he had at USC. I think the staff will likely get back to that Dickey-Williams rotation as soon as possible.” Texas Tech is second in FBS in passes intercepted (13) but has also given up 16 TD passes and is ranked third-worst in the Big 12 in pass defense. How do you expect the defense to try and stop Noah Fifita? “As mentioned above, the Texas Tech defense last year was getting to the quarterback so quickly that teams simply could not function offensively. This year . . . not so much. Fifita has rounded out to be such a good quarterback, I truly expect him to have a very good day. There’s almost no difference between his home and road stats, three picks on the road and just one at home, and he’s throwing for nearly 300 yards every time he steps on the field. That’s the kind of consistency that you expect from a senior and with Fifita’s ability to run to keep the defense honest, I expect him to do what he’s done all year long.” Who are the top defensive players that Arizona has to be most concerned with? “Defensive tackle AJ Holmes is an absolute unit and there aren’t a ton of defensive tackles that truly rush the passer, but he’s one of them. The linebacking corps is incredibly solid with Ben Roberts, John Curry and Austin Romaine. I’ll also add in Brice Pollock at cornerback. The pass defense is struggling a bit, but he’s a solid cornerback that can make plays.” Considering all the money that was spent on this team, and all the national attention it has brought on itself—thanks, Cody Campbell!—does it feel like the season is on the line in this game? How do you expect Tech to respond to that last performance? “As you have already recognized, this team is a quarterback short of maybe what it could have been. I try not to involve myself in the offseason drama. The whole thing was a mess and handled poorly. I think we’ve all moved on, but I know it still lingers and I think that Sorsby would have made a significant difference in the offense. For what Joey McGuire preaches, yes, the season is on the brink because the goal is to win the Big 12 and make the playoffs. I don’t know that a Big 12 team with two losses makes the playoff and I also don’t think that a 2-loss Big 12 team makes the championship. “I do expect Texas Tech to play much better than what they did against Cincinnati and I think it will be a much more competitive game. I also realize that Arizona’s defense is no joke and the Texas Tech offense has really only played well against defenses that aren’t very good. The offense and defense for the Red Raiders have a lot to prove against Arizona.” Prediction time. Does Arizona end the Red Raiders’ 12-game home win streak and continue its push toward the Big 12 title game or does Texas Tech get back on track? Give us a score pick. “My gut tells me that this will be an incredibly close game and Vegas thinks so as well. With a touchdown advantage, the line now sits at Texas Tech -3.5. I tend to agree, that despite the flaws that were on display against Cincinnati, I think Texas Tech does win the game, but I’d take Arizona and those points. Something like 37-34 is what I see the final score being.” Next 3 weeks could decide Big 12 football title game participants Download the new SB Nation app All of your communities in one place. He was limited in practice all week, donning a yellow non-contact jersey in all three sessions. There's no time to sulk over losses or complain about things not working out. Another week presents another tough test and an opportunity to right the ship. The Iowa Hawkeyes are back in action against the Wisconsin Badgers for the Battle of the Heartland, so let's dig in. Iowa lost its last outing to Minnesota in one of the sloppiest games the Hawkeyes have played under Kirk Ferentz in years. Wisconsin, on the other hand, comes to Kinnick Stadium fresh off a very strong showing in a win against USC. Iowa vs Wisconsin betting odds, spread, total Spread: Iowa -3.5 (-105), Wisconsin +3.5 (-115) Money Line: Iowa -170, Wisconsin +142 Total: Over 36.5 (-112), Under 36.5 (-108) Odds are courtesy of DraftKings Iowa opened as 4.5-point favorites, so there has been some slight movement toward Wisconsin, but nothing drastic in the overall feel of Iowa being the home favorite this week. Riley Donald's Iowa vs Wisconsin Prediction Prediction: Iowa 17, Wisconsin 13 I have no reason to believe we are going to see offensive fireworks in this game. Iowa knows the advantage its defense has over Wisconsin's offense and vice versa. These offenses are going to come out cautiously, not looking to make the big turnover that puts them behind. It's a classic Iowa game, really. Iowa is going to turn this to its defense, let the punt unit do its job of pinning Wisconsin deep, and find just enough juice via one or two big plays or short fields set up by winning the turnover battle. More than anything, Iowa is simply elite after a loss under Kirk Ferentz. This game has all the makings of an inspired performance from the Hawkeyes after doing everything wrong last week. Iowa gets back on track with a gritty, old-school Big Ten rivalry win. Iowa uses all of its usual tricks of suffocating the offense, doing the little things right, and making life hard on Wisconsin. picks.headline: 3 Bold Predictions for Iowa Football vs. Wisconsin in the Battle for the Heartland
picks.blurb: 3 Bold Predictions for Iowa Football vs. Wisconsin in the Battle for the Heartland Skip to main content SI.COM SPRING SPORTS HAWKEYENATION SI.COM HAWKEYES FB SI.COM HAWKEYES BB BASKETBALL BASKETBALL NEWS MEN'S SCHEDULE MEN'S RANKINGS FOOTBALL NEWS While the Floyd of Rosedale slipped out of the Iowa Hawkeyes ' grasp, another trophy is on the line this week when the Wisconsin Badgers come to Kinnick Stadium in Iowa City, Iowa. The Battle for the Heartland trophy is going to be up for grabs. Iowa has dominated the Badgers for the last two seasons in two blowout wins, but this year looks like it will be a different type of game. These teams mirror each other quite well. Both play good defense, want to run the ball, and are winning games. It figures to be a four-quarter battle in this rivalry. Iowa holds Wisconsin under 150 yards passing This is a day when Iowa's secondary can shine, as we have seen in so many previous seasons. The group looks strong, led by Zach Lutmer. Outside, Jaylen Watson and Deshaun Lee are playing at a really high level, while Xavier Styles is growing each week at safety. Phil Parker is going to have Iowa containing Colton Joseph in the pocket, forcing him to beat Iowa with his arm. If Iowa can corral him and make him make tight-window throws all game, it's going to be a long day of incompletions and potentially some turnovers. DJ Vonnahme leads Iowa's passing game My gut tells me that Iowa's offense is going to have a very "2024" feel to it, like it did with Kaleb Johnson and all of the under-center zone runs. This is where DJ Vonnahme can feast. He can be the easy, big target for Hank Brown off of heavy play-action when the defense starts to flow. Iowa should look to Vonnahme early and often to get him the ball and set him up to run after the catch. When found in passing situations, I really like DJ Vonnahme down the seam. He can run and carry this route, plus he has the feel to find green grass between the linebackers and safeties. Iowa averages more yards per rush than Wisconsin Hear me out for one second - neither run game is going to be overly pretty in this game. Just prepare yourselves for that. These defenses are going to commit so many resources to stopping the run that even if responsibilities are messed up, there will be backup on standby to clean up the mess. I think Iowa's defense is going to eliminate much of the success for Wisconsin by containing Colton Joseph, which is a specialty of Phil Parker, and therefore force the backs to make something happen. Iowa can stop the run in its base defense, which it should be in for most of this game. Offensively, it won't be pretty for Iowa, but I think the Hawkeyes have a spirited run game that converts some ugly short-yardage plays and stays patient enough to get a few chunks from the running back room. It will take time, but Iowa's run game gets going just enough in this one. The Badger program was seemingly going nowhere under head coach Luke Fickell, and many people believed 2026 would be Fickell's final season before the school would cut ties with him. But flash-forward to Halloween, and Iowa and Wisconsin enter this matchup in completely different directions. The Hawkeyes are desperate for a bounce-back win after an ugly loss at Minnesota last weekend, while the Badgers could vault themselves into College Football Playoff contention with a victory (just check their schedule after the Iowa game). Every Iowa-Wisconsin game always seems to provide something unusual, so one can only imagine what will happen on Saturday. Here's my prediction for the matchup. Matchup: No. 25 Wisconsin Badgers (5-2, 3-1) @ Iowa Hawkeyes (5-2, 2-2) Location: Kinnick Stadium in Iowa City, Iowa Scheduled game time: Oct. 31 at 11:10 a.m. Weather: 63 degrees Announcers: Gus Johnson (play-by-play), Joel Klatt (analyst), Jenny Taft (sideline) Radio: Hawkeye Radio Network (Gary Dolphin, Pat Angerer) Student Radio: KRUI (Collin Carrithers, Luke Jorden) I'm very surprised that Wisconsin is a competitive team at this point, but Iowa Everywhere's Chris Hassel said it best on Wednesday - the Badgers know their identity by now and the Hawkeyes don't. Iowa essentially using a roulette wheel to determine its starting quarterback each week has clearly caused this offense to be inconsistent week in and week out. Though Wisconsin hasn't received great quarterback play from Old Dominion transfer Colton Joseph, it has relied on a good run game and excellent defense to win football games. Sticking to that strategy has worked well for the Badgers. All you have to do to figure that out is go back and watch their last game against USC. Wisconsin dominated both lines of scrimmage en route to a 24-7 victory last weekend and you better believe they'll try and do the same thing to Iowa. But can the Badgers actually come to Kinnick Stadium and pull this one out? The momentum is definitely on Wisconsin's side of the ball, but if there's one edge Iowa has, it's the fact that it's playing at Kinnick Stadium. The Badgers haven't won in Iowa City since 2018, with the Hawkeyes winning the last three games in Kinnick by a combined score of 94-27. I don't expect a lot of points to be scored in this one (stay tuned for my betting prediction later today), but if there's one thing I know about Kirk Ferentz, it's his ability to win these Big Ten grinders. He's going to try and flip the calendar back to 2023 and win this game with complimentary football. That wouldn't be a good strategy on the road, but I think this defense will feed off the home crowd and give their offense enough short fields to secure a narrow victory. The Hawkeyes take down Wisconsin for the sixth time in seven games. Prediction: Iowa 16, Wisconsin 13

picks.headline: Iowa Hawkeyes Football: Wisconsin Badgers Game Preview
picks.blurb: Iowa Hawkeyes Football: Wisconsin Badgers Game Preview - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football College Football Playoff NFL injury tracker Belichick-Hudson breakup Brewers' championship parade Chet Holmgren injury Fantasy Start 'Em, Sit 'Em Iowa Hawkeyes Football: Wisconsin Badgers Game Preview David Fidler Fri, October 30, 2026 at 11:00 AM UTC · 8 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads This Saturday, the 5-2 Iowa Hawkeyes are back at home in Kinnick Stadium to take on the 5-2 Wisconsin Badgers in the Battle for the Heartland Trophy. The Badgers, whose only losses are to ranked teams, are trending in the right direction while Iowa, which just lost to a mediocre Minnesota, is trending in the wrong direction. It's hard to know what to expect from the Hawkeyes going into this game. The team that embarrassed itself against the Gophers would lose to the Badgers and probably all the rest of the teams on its schedule. On the other hand, the team that showed up three weeks ago against the Washington Huskies would compete with the Badgers and have a reasonable chance of running the rest of the schedule. My guess is that the Hawkeyes that show up this week and for the rest of the year will be somewhere in the middle of those two extremes. Will the Hawkeyes Bounce Back? It is hard to remember Iowa looking more lackluster, more undisciplined, against an inferior opponent than it looked against Minnesota. It did almost everything it could to hand the game to the Gophers. The offense, to a man, looked unprepared. The special teams was uneven with a couple of huge gaffes. The defense did enough to win, but even Iowa's vaunted defense had at least two notable breakdowns. This game against the Badgers is important not only for Iowa's record, not only to preserve its slim playoff hopes, but it will also say what this team is made of. After a performance like the one against Minnesota, when everything was in the line, it would be easy enough for the Hawkeyes to give up on the season. On the other hand, they could also look adversity in the face and come out swinging. If the Hawkeyes show up flat again, it is entirely possible the season could spiral. Either way, there is a lot to answer for this week. Can Iowa Play a Clean Game? Iowa currently ranks 40th in the NCAA in penalty-yards-per-game. That's not terrible, but in 2025 the Hawkeyes were third. 2024: third. 2023 and 2022: fifth. 2021: sixth. 2020: 14th. You get the idea. Interestingly, the last time Iowa didn't finish the season in the top 25 of fewest penalty yards was 2015 when they went undefeated, but the 2026 Hawkeyes decidedly don't have CJ Beathard at quarterback. The larger point is that Iowa plays clean football. It is a hallmark of the program under Kirk Ferentz, and this incarnation of the Iowa Hawkeyes has not played clean football. It was evident against Minnesota, but it's been evident all season. And then there's turnover margin. After the garbage that was the Minnesota game, Iowa finds itself 80th in the country with a turnover margin of -1. The reality is Iowa can't sustain undisciplined, sloppy play. It can't give the opposing team free drives. It can't give the opposing team free yards. More than anything else, that needs to be cleaned up, and it needs to be cleaned up before anything else. As long as that is part of this team's DNA, it's not going to win football games. Who is the Quarterback and Can He Finish the Game? You've seen, and/or made your feelings known on the message boards. Hank Brown should have started, Jeremy Hecklinski should have never been benched, Heck should have come back in after Brown proved ineffective, etc. I have my opinions, but I don't know if it's the right choice any more than any of the others. What I do know is that Brown has had approximately five bad quarters in a row absent one drive. And against Minnesota, Heck was in his own head, making terrible decisions and starting to spiral. In short, Iowa seems to have two pretty poor quarterbacks that it has to decide between. Maybe that's why Ferentz has been so reticent to commit to one. Whomever the quarterback is, he doesn't need to be the second coming of Tom Brady. For the first time in a long time, Iowa has playmakers at receiver, not to mention the usual array of solid tight ends. All the quarterback has to do is make the makeables. When he has an open tight end in the seam on third-and-6, he has to hit him. When he has a receiver heading toward the end zone with five steps on his defender, he cannot underthrow him and give the defensive back a chance. He can't throw into double coverage. He can't hold the ball too long and take sacks. Given the running game, or lack thereof, a lot of weight is on the quarterback's shoulders, maybe too much. But with a good defense, all he has to do is consistently make the makeables. 2 Things to Watch Iowa fumbled five times vs Minnesota. Five?!?! Four were official and one didn't count due to a penalty. Okay, five was probably an anomaly, but at least one part of that equation is not an anomaly. Evan James, the punt returner, who fumbled the one against Minnesota that was called back due to a penalty, has fumbled three punts this season. He has fielded 32 punts. That means he's fumbling at a rate of almost 10% of his punts. Call me crazy but that is too much. I might be misremembering but I can swear Kirk Ferentz took Desmond King (Thorpe Award winner Desmond King!) off punt duties for flubbing a punt once during his sophomore year. Evan James has three fumbles, and he is still listed as the starting punt returner against Wisconsin. I'm all for Ferentz changing his approach to coaching here and there, but I don't think his leniency with fumbleitis is a positive development. It's hard to predict interceptions as the quarterback situation is still a bit hazy, but assuming it's Hank Brown, he did avoid the interception bug through the first four games, but since, he threw one against OSU and two against Minnesota. Then there's the defense. Look, the defense has done enough to win games—it certainly did enough against Minnesota—but it hasn't been generating a high number of turnovers. The Iowa defense has generated three interceptions against five Power-Four opponents this year. All of them have been by senior cornerback Deshaun Lee who, as I noted last week , is the only member of the secondary who is meeting the admittedly lofty expectations of an Iowa defensive back. This is a good week to generate turnovers as Wisconsin doesn't have a very good offense, and quarterback Colton Jones, though he is dangerous with his legs, is not a good passer. Jones has thrown five interceptions, but none in the last three games. However, that's largely because he hasn't put the ball in the air very much in the past three games, only averaging 16.7 attempts per game. The opportunities for interceptions should be there if Iowa can put the Badgers in a position where they have to throw the ball. I've already said that Iowa had to play a clean game. That includes winning the turnover battle. The Offensive Gameplan Iowa has played five Power-Four opponents. It has been able to run successfully and consistently against one of them. With a 20% success rate, I am going to assume Iowa will not be able to run the football using its base offense until proven otherwise. This is especially true after the announcement that starting tailback Kamari Moulton is out for the season. But the offense still needs to move the ball. Offenses typically have a play that the entire offense is built around. It's not the home run play or a play saved for special occasions. It's a bread-and-butter play that is run 5-15 times a game, is safe and nets consistent and dependable yardage. For Iowa, that play has historically been the inside zone, but it's not working, and as the Hawkeyes can't depend on big chunk plays through the passing game, they will need a play to build the offense around. So what's it going to be? Sweeps to the receivers, the screen game, the read option? None of it's ideal and it's not possible for Iowa to just scrap the inside zone, the foundation of its offense, in the middle of the season. However, running into a wall 5-10 times a game and averaging 1-2 yards per carry is not a winning formula, especially when the quarterbacks don't seem capable of carrying the offense on their shoulders. 1 Crazy Prediction I predict Iowa won't fumble the ball five times. Sounds like a pretty gutless prediction until you look at last week. But my serious prediction is that the Hawkeyes generate a non-offensive touchdown. Special teams? Maybe they keep the pick-6 streak alive? In truth, I think they might need it to win because I have no faith in this offense against a good Badger defense.

away.blurb: Iowa will be trying to replace the production of Kamari Moulton, who is out for the season after suffering an injury against Minnesota . Moulton leads Iowa in carries (86), rushing yards (541) and rushing touchdowns (four) this season. Phillips ran for nearly 2,000 yards at FCS South Dakota last season and has the potential to provide serious firepower on the ground. But that hasn’t materialized so far this season. He missed time due to injury earlier this season and has been limited to 25 carries for just 88 yards. His best game came against Washington, when he ran 10 times for 42 yards. Moulton's injury could also open the door for others like Braeden Jackson, Nathan McNeil and Xavier Williams. picks.headline: Ole Miss vs. Auburn Predictions: Our Staff Picks the Winner and Final Score
picks.blurb: Ole Miss vs. Auburn Predictions: Our Staff Picks the Winner and Final Score Skip to main content SI.COM FOOTBALL FOOTBALL NEWS BASKETBALL NEWS No. 12 Ole Miss is playing back in Oxford on Halloween weekend to take on an Auburn team in the midst of its first season led by Alex Golesh. Both teams are entering Week 9 coming off losses, but it’s the Rebels that are playing with pressure for their playoff lives moving forward. Though Auburn is sitting at 4-3 (2-3) through what’s been an up and down season up to this point, the Tigers are no slouch. Just two weeks ago Auburn went into Athens and pulled out a last-second win over Georgia. Kickoff between the Rebels and Tigers is set for 11:45 a.m. CT on the SEC Network. Ole Miss will enter game day as a double-digit home favorite. Ahead of the Rebels' latest conference matchup, Ole Miss On SI predicts which team wins and why. Oct 24, 2026; Austin, Texas, USA; Mississippi Rebels quarterback Trinidad Chambliss (6) warms up before the game against the Texas Longhorns at Darrell K Royal-Texas Memorial Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Scott Wachter-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Tyler Komis Not that it matters by any means, but aside from its impressive road win against Georgia two weeks ago, nothing particularly jumps off the page to me about Alex Golesh’s first team at Auburn. That’s not to say Golesh isn’t the right fit for the job either. He has the Tigers sitting above .500 and is working through his first season as a head coach at a Power Four program. As it pertains to the game itself, I expect Ole Miss to maintain its home win streak that dates back to September of the 2024 season. This certainly should be a focused group after picking up its second loss in Texas last weekend and they can’t afford to overlook Auburn even though Georgia is around the corner. Controlling their playoff destiny is on thin ice. Trinidad Chambliss could use a bounce back game after not looking like himself the past two weeks. Considering Auburn’s weaker pass defense through its secondary, I believe Chambliss does what he desperately needs to do and may even incorporate his legs more than usual. Ole Miss needs to prove it can find a faster start on the offensive side of the ball as a whole. Defensively, Ole Miss should match up well against an offense that has already surrendered 29 sacks (4.3 per game) if the unit can contain Byrum Brown. The Tigers’ quarterback leads the team in rushing yards, but still looks like a signal-caller in his first season in the SEC. Ole Miss 31, Auburn 17 While Auburn is more than capable of pulling off the upset, just look at its victory over No. 3 Georgia in Athens, I don’t see it happening this Saturday. Against Texas, the Ole Miss offense did everything it could to let Texas pull away. However, despite struggling for most of the night, they lost the game by just seven points. The two games prior to Texas, Ole Miss won by blowing out its opponents. With the Rebels’ back against the wall and needing to go on a win streak if they want to make the College Football Playoff, I think they win easily against Auburn and carry some nice momentum into their matchup against the Georgia Bulldogs next Saturday night. Ole Miss 34, Auburn 17 Cooper Ferguson Alex Golesh will take this Auburn team to greener pastures than Hugh Freeze ever did, and I think that in the alternate universe where Golesh came to Auburn, things worked out. A great coach tasked with waking a sleeping giant, I think Auburn will, in due time, become a force to be reckoned with again in the SEC. That time is not now, though. Florida and the first half against Texas need to be remembered as blips in a strong season for the Rebels in years to come. With a strong showing against Auburn this Halloween, Ole Miss will be well on its way to correcting its path. Chambliss and Co. dispatch the Tigers easily, and Ole Miss moves on to prep for Georgia. Ole Miss 49, Auburn 14 Billy Flowers Byrum Brown will be a major problem for the Ole Miss run defense, but Auburn's offensive line is horrific. I think the Tigers' only path to victory is through Brown's legs, which, frankly, will not put enough points on the board for Auburn. I think Trinidad bounces back, and Makhai Frazier has a breakout performance against the Tiger's less-than-stellar rush defense. I do think Auburn can keep the game close, thanks to their rushing attack. The Ole Miss offense is too talented, and the Tigers won't score enough to match it. Ole Miss 38, Auburn 27 Zion Trammell Ole Miss is coming off a disappointing performance against Texas and really needs a solid response this week. The key to victory is to keep Byrum Brown in the pocket. The Auburn quarterback can make big plays with his legs, so limiting his mobility will be a priority. The Tigers knocked off Georgia a couple of weeks ago, but I think Pete Golding’s team responds well at home. Ole Miss 38, Auburn 24 The Ole Miss Rebels face a must-win game against the Auburn Tigers. They won't disappoint. Auburn is a dangerous football team, but Ole Miss will show its talent when it needs to. Trinidad Chambliss will have a day as the defense struggles at first but settles in. The Rebels, in the end, will win this game by three-plus touchdowns. Ole Miss 45, Auburn 24 Published 15 hours ago TYLER KOMIS Bio: Tyler Komis is a beat reporter for Ole Miss On SI. He is a Biletnikoff Award and Lombardi Award voter from New Jersey with more than five years of sports reporting experience. Prior to joining On SI, he previously covered Ole Miss Athletics for 247Sports (2021-2026), chronicling the ascension of the football program and the beginning of its coaching transition to Pete Golding ahead of the 2025-26 College Football Playoffs. A matchup that could help Auburn pull off an upset victory over Ole Miss is in the run game. The Rebels are at the bottom of the SEC, giving up 161.1 yards per game on the ground. With the new season comes a new series on AL.com where each week, our Auburn beat writers will predict the result of the upcoming game. Be sure to join in on the fun and make your predictions down below in our comment section: Jerry Humphrey III Tracker : 5-2 Score: Ole Miss 35, Auburn 21 Analysis: Auburn needs its face back after getting bullied off the field in its 38-17 loss to LSU. However, it will not be easy when matching against No. 12 Ole Miss and quarterback Trinidad Chambliss. The Tigers' have given up 2,778 opponent yards through seven games this season, as Chambliss ranks second in the SEC in passing with 1,926 yards. This game will come down to if Auburn can make stops on defense because after giving up over 500 yards of offense to LSU. Chambliss also comes into the game with seven interceptions after throwing two in the Rebels' 34-27 loss to Texas last week. Auburn has eight interceptions and four forced fumbles this year despite the up-and-down play on that side of the ball. Forcing turnovers will be the recipe the Tigers' follow in their efforts to spoil Halloween in Oxford. Peter Rauterkus Tracker : 6-1 Score: Ole Miss 35, Auburn 24 Analysis: Auburn's trip to Oxford this weekend marks the end of a brutal four-game stretch during the month of October. The Tigers found a way to pull off a shocking upset over Georgia two weeks ago and will need a similar effort to do the same against Ole Miss. The Rebels don't seem to be as talented as Georgia but are a double-digit favorite for a reason. Auburn's defense hasn't done much this season to make me believe it can slow down Trinidad Chambliss, Ole Miss' superstar quarterback. If Auburn can run the ball, it has a chance to put up points on Ole Miss' defense. That's been the Rebels' biggest weakness through seven games. Even if Auburn does that, it's going to take some Ole Miss turnovers and a few good breaks for this game to go the Tigers' way. I think Auburn keeps this game competitive but won't have enough defensively to pull off another road upset.

away.headline: Auburn head coach Alex Golesh gives key injury update on Tai Buster
away.blurb: Sophomore Tai Buster was expected to be a key piece of Auburn's offensive line rotation this season, but a preseason setback has kept him away from the field . This week, Auburn head coach Alex Golesh gave a positive report for Buster's availability, saying he could be available to play as early as a few weeks. “Tai (Buster) has worked his tail off. I give Tai a lot of credit. He is working through return to play," Golesh said Monday. "The hope is that here in a couple of weeks, we get him fully integrated in practice, and it gives us a chance to see where he is." For injured players, it can take days or weeks to catch up and return to their routine, but Golesh says that will not be the case for Buster. Buster has remained immersed in practice and should return to full speed quickly. "He’s been engaged; I give him a lot of credit again, he’s been engaged," Golesh said. "He’s itching to get back out there. I thought when he got banged up, he was competing at a high level. We’re excited to get him back here soon.” Adding Buster to the rotation will not solve every issue the offensive line faces, but having an extra body will help keep linemen, especially at guard, fresh during Auburn's final stretch of regular-season games. The Tigers will be without Buster for their next game, Saturday at Ole Miss, but he could return in November to assist Auburn with their pursuit of bowl eligibility. home.headline: Top Auburn WR Listed as Questionable Ahead of Ole Miss Matchup
home.blurb: Top Auburn WR Listed as Questionable Ahead of Ole Miss Matchup Skip to main content SI.COM Koger was listed as questionable on the Tigers’ initial injury report Thursday meaning that he has around a 50% chance to play, while offensive lineman Tai Buster and tight end Hunter Herring are listed as out. At this time, it is unclear as to why exactly Koger is listed as questionable, but it goes without saying that losing his production would be a significant blow for the Tigers, as he currently ranks third among all Tigers in total receiving yards. Koger was a four-star recruit out of St. Frances Academy in Baltimore, Maryland, when he signed with Alex Golesh and the USF Bulls, earning playing time quite early in his young career. Last season, his freshman year, Koger hauled in 38 Byrum Brown passes for 597 yards and eight touchdowns before transferring to the Plains this past offseason. If Koger is ruled out for the game against Ole Miss, the Tigers still have plenty of other talent to turn to in the interim, including fellow USF transfer receiver Christian Neptune, who completed a touchdown pass to Singleton against Georgia, as well as DeShawn Spencer, a true freshman who has hauled in 10 passes for 90 yards and two touchdowns so far this season. The Auburn Tigers are looking to rebound from a devastating loss to LSU, in which the Bayou Bengals came to town and routed the home team by 21 points, though that effort may get a little more difficult with the potential absence of one key wide receiver: Jeremiah Koger. The Maryland native was highly anticipated on the Plains and has lived up to a large part of those expectations, though he has not yet quite turned in the statistical production of the Tigers’ top two receivers, Keshaun Singleton and Chas Nimrod, both of whom are also new Auburn transfers from USF. So far this season, Koger has caught 14 passes for 230 yards, both stats ranking third on the team. Notably, however, Koger has yet to bring in a touchdown for the Tigers this year, which is quite surprising given his production at USF last season. Singleton and Nimrod have worked to make up for that, though, hauling in a combined five touchdown passes from Brown this season. They’ve also combined for 69 total receptions and 771 receiving yards, a high mark for any Auburn duo. The Tigers are scheduled to square off against Ole Miss this Saturday, October 31, at 11:45 a.m. CT, in a matchup that is scheduled to be broadcast on SEC Network. home.headline: Ole Miss announces major injury news before facing Georgia
home.blurb: Ole Miss announces major injury news before facing Georgia - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF Brewers' championship parade Fantasy Start 'Em, Sit 'Em Ole Miss announces major injury news before facing Georgia Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads The Georgia Bulldogs (6-1, 4-1 SEC) face tough tests against two currently ranked teams the next two weeks. They face Florida on Halloween and play at the Ole Miss Rebels (5-2, 3-2) on Nov. 7. However, the Rebels may be without one of their star players. Ole Miss coach Pete Golding announced running back Kewan Lacy had dislocated his shoulder and will be sidelined for the team's game against Auburn this week. The injury puts him at risk of also missing the game against Georgia . Lacy suffered the injury in Ole Miss's 34-27 loss to Texas last week. It's the same shoulder he injured in Ole Miss' win against LSU that caused him to miss the game against Florida. He first injured his shoulder in last year's College Football Playoff win over Tulane. While he stayed active during the rest of Ole Miss's run to the CFP semifinal, he underwent offseason surgery. Lacy had a breakout sophomore season for Ole Miss in 2025. He registered 1,567 yards and 24 touchdowns on 306 carries. He played twice against Georgia, recording 31 yards and two touchdowns on 12 carries in the regular-season loss and another 98 yards and two touchdowns on 22 carries in Ole Miss's Sugar Bowl win. This season, he has 388 yards and five touchdowns on 78 carries in six games. Lacy was a first-team preseason All-SEC pick. Ole Miss struggled without him in their 52-28 loss to Florida. Georgia fans will keep his status in mind after they face Florida. While EverBank Stadium in Jacksonville undergoes renovation, the game is taking a two game hiatus from Duval County. The game will take place in Mercedes-Benz stadium in Atlanta on Saturday. Depending on the weather, the roof could be closed, hence the party being inside. This will be a very different atmosphere for this historic rivalry. Now, Florida fans will see that Jacksonville is not that neutral of a site. Atlanta is the equivalent in Georgia. So, that means some ridiculous things could happen Saturday afternoon. Here are three bold predictions for Saturday: Gunner Stockton Totals 4 Touchdowns Gunner Stockton is coming off of the worst game of his life, where he turned the ball over three times for the first time in his career, including the untimely fumble at the end of the game. That fumble led to Auburn’s game-winning field goal. Florida has the second worst passing defense in the SEC. Stockton is one of the best and most efficient quarterbacks in the nation. A bounce back game seems likely, and he will total at least four scores. Georgia Wins Turnover Margin by 2 The Dawgs lost the turnover battle to Auburn 0-3, and they almost won. Georgia has been better about creating turnover opportunities this year than it was last season. Georgia has also had a knack for winning games despite losing the turnover battle. This game last year is an example of that. Georgia is due for a big turnover game. The Dawgs only have two takeaways over the last three games. Jadan Baugh Gets His Jadan Baugh is arguably college football’s best running back. He has simmered down since his 600-yard and 11-touchdown start over the first four games. Rushing for over 90 yards and a score en route to an upset road win over Texas can be considered a bounce back. Georgia’s run defense has progressively gotten worse as the season has gone on. Alabama was able to rip off some expl;osive and total about 160 yards on the ground. Byrum Brown ran all over the Dawgs, helping Auburn total over 190 rushing yards. Baugh is good enough to get his. Georgia is good enough to win even if that happens. I think he will have around 100 total yards and a score. picks.blurb: Odds Have Changed for Georgia Football vs. Florida Gators Skip to main content SI.COM SI.COM BULLDOGS FB SI.COM BULLDOGS BB FOOTBALL FOOTBALL NEWS BASKETBALL NEWS ATHENS - Odds have been updated to Georgia Football’s massive clash with the Florida Gators 48 hours before the rivals face off in Atlanta. The Bulldogs and Gators are playing a one-off game in Atlanta this season , and one next year in Tampa as Jacksonville (the traditional home for this game) rebuilds its stadium. The anticipation for the game is growing as the weekend grows near. What’s also growing is the betting line for the game. On Sunday FanDuel listed the Bulldogs as a 9.5-point favorite over the Gators. DraftKings had UGA as a 10.5-point favorite in the contest. Both betting houses now have Georgia as a 12.5-point favorite to win the game. The move in the line is a fairly significant one - placing the game firmly into double-digit territory. Of course, betting lines are only an indication of what experts feel is expected to happen - they are not a guarantee of an outcome. There are two reasons the line has be crept up over the week. First, both of Florida’s quarterbacks are injured in some form. Athens-area native Aaron Philo started the first six games of the Gators’ season, but missed Florida’s 27-24 win at Texas with a shoulder injury. Tramell Jones started for the Gators in that game and guided the Gators to an upset in Austin. Jones has “wear-and-tear” injuries. Georgia football TE Jaden Reddell celebrates with Georgia football RB Chauncey Bowens after scoring a touchdown against Vanderbilt. | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Florida coach Jon Sumrall said Monday that he would not name a starter at that time. Florida coach Jon Sumrall said Monday that he would not name a starter at that time. “Both guys are available - believe in both guys,” Sumrall told reporters. “Not going to name a starter today. We need both those guys to be ready to play.” Both Gator quarterbacks were listed as questionable Wednesday night on the SEC’s mandated injury report. In addition, Georgia got very good news with an upgrade for running back Chauncey Bowens, who was upgraded to questionable from out, which is where he’s been the last few weeks. Bowens scored the game-winning touchdown against the Gators last year in Jacksonville. Second, there was likely some overreaction to Georgia’s upset loss to Auburn at home, and the Gators’ upset win on the road at Florida. Most of the summer this game was listed around the 12-point mark. Florida’s play early in the season dropped the number under ten points, but that recovered to back over double digits after Florida was blown out in back-to-back losses to Missouri and South Carolina. But only twice in modern history has a double-digit favorite lost this game (1997 and 2014). In both upsets turnovers and a robust run game powered the underdog to an unexpected win. Since 2010, the Bulldogs have been favored to beat the Gators 13 times in the last 16 games. Georgia is 11-5 straight up against the Gators since then - losing in overtime as a one-point favorite in 2010, a 10-point favorite in 2014, a 3-point underdog in 2015, a 6.5-point underdog in 2016 and a 3-point favorite in 2020. On average the Dawgs have been a 6.5-point favorite to beat Florida since 2010. The team that runs the ball better in the World’s Largest Outdoor Cocktail Party is 15-1 since 2010 (2020 - Florida, 44-28). Odds refresh periodically and are subject to change. For the first time in the history of the World's Largest Outdoor Cocktail Party, Florida and Georgia will play in Atlanta at Mercedes-Benz Stadium, with kickoff slated for Saturday at 3:30 p.m. ET (ABC). The Bulldogs are 11.5-point favorites, and my Florida vs. Georgia prediction and college football picks expect Kirby Smart's team to take advantage of Jon Sumrall's defense in his first Cocktail Party. Who will win Florida vs Georgia: Georgia -11.5 Kirby Smart has owned the Florida vs. Georgia rivalry recently, winning eight of the last nine games. While he's just 5-4 against the spread in those games, his Bulldogs have the advantage against a sporadic Florida team. But without knowing which version of Florida we'll get, I would only take the Bulldogs up to -12.5 . Georgia's defense is far more trustworthy than Florida's, ranking 14th nationally in available yards percentage (35.7%) , 21st in defensive success rate (35.4%), and holding six of seven opponents to 20 or fewer points. With athletes like Chris Cole and Ellis Robinson IV, Georgia is well-equipped to deal with Buster Faulkner's misdirection-heavy offense. Plus, the Gators' top two QBs ( Aaron Philo , Tramell Jones Jr. ) are questionable , and while I expect them to play, it could impact their consistency. In a high-scoring game, Georgia's defense will make enough stops to cover. TOP PICK Florida vs Georgia Over/Under pick: Over 54.5 Georgia has been an Over machine this season, hitting it in six of seven games, despite its defense allowing just 15.9 points per game. I like the Over to hit at 55.5 or better for the fifth time in the last seven Cocktail Parties, especially given Faulkner's familiarity with Smart and Georgia's defense. Faulkner worked for Smart at Georgia for three years before spending the last three seasons as Georgia Tech's offensive coordinator; his offenses averaged 24.6 points and 392 yards against the Bulldogs. With one of the top running backs in the country in Jadan Baugh , who ranks top 10 in forced missed tackles (40), Florida should score 20+. Its defense will do the rest of the job for the Over. Florida has one of the worst defenses in the Power Four, r anking 125th in the country in defensive success rate (49.5%) , and it hasn't played an offense as efficient as Georgia's yet this season. Florida vs Georgia combo Some weeks Florida looks like a College Football Playoff team (against Ole Miss and Texas ), and other weeks it looks like it might not win eight games (against Missouri and South Carolina ). Which version will come to play in the World's Largest Cocktail Party? If Auburn hadn't improbably upset the Bulldogs the last time they played, they would probably be closer to 14.5-point favorites because of Florida's defensive struggles and offensive injuries. Coming out of a bye, I expect Smart to have Georgia ready to roll in a rivalry game he's dominated and to pull away in the second half against a Florida defense that ranks second-worst in havoc rate in the SEC (14.5%). "We've shown our guys clips of him since the start of the year to say are you practicing to tackle him, or are you practicing to tackle who you're playing against?" Smart said. "He likes to jump cut, he's a physical back," Georgia linebacker Raylen Wilson said. "He's a good player. He likes to run that ball and we like to stop the run." away.blurb: News Sports Opinion Guardian Real Estate Advertise Obituaries eNewspaper Legals FOOTBALL Florida football injury update | Two QBs listed as questionable for Georgia Kevin Brockway Gainesville Sun Updated Oct. 28, 2026, 8:56 p.m. ET Florida football made its quarterback situation even more cloudy heading into its matchup against rival Georgia in Atlanta. The top two Florida Gators quarterbacks on the depth chart − Aaron Philio and Tramell Jones Jr.−are both listed as questionable for UF's showdown with the Bulldogs. Philo, who started UF's first six games for the Gators , sat out Florida 's game against Texas on October 17 with a shoulder injury. Jones, who led UF to an upset win over the Longhorns by passing for 155 yards and 2 TDs, is dealing with an undisclosed injury. "He’s got a couple of bumps and bruises, too, now," Sumrall said. "And he had, you know, pulled the guy fresh out of that garage and he goes and plays, and he got a couple fender-benders. So, there's some bumps and bruises he's dealing with that are new. I noticed it last week." Also on the availability report, inside linebacker Jaden Robinson and wide receiver Bailey Stockton are listed as doubtful for UF, while running back Duke Clark has been upgraded to questionable. Wide receiver Vernell Brown III, who has missed UF's last three games with a knee strain, is listed as probable. For Georgia, wide receiver Thomas Blackshear, outside linebacker Amaris Williams and safety Tyriq Green have been ruled out. Preseason All-SEC safety KJ Bolden is listed as questionable, along with running back Chauncey Bowens and wide receiver Isiah Canon. Florida coach Jon Sumrall said both practiced this week and hinted Jones was dealing with issues following the Texas win during his opening week press conference on October 26. If Jones and Philo both can't go, Florida would turn to its third-string quarterback, redshirt junior Aidan Warner, or true freshman Will Griffin. Warner appeared in the Florida-Georgia game in 2024 when DJ Lagway went down with a hamstring injury and made one career start the following week at Texas. No. 20 Florida (5-2. 3-2 SEC) is looking to break five-game losing streak against the Bulldogs (6-1, 4-1 SEC) when the two schools meet on Saturday, October 31 (3:30 p.m., ABC). The game, traditionally held in Jacksonville, was moved to Mercedes-Benz Stadium in Atlanta due to the $1.4 billion renovation at EverBank Stadium for the NFL's Jacksonville Jaguars. home.blurb: News Sports Opinion Guardian Real Estate Advertise Obituaries eNewspaper Legals FOOTBALL Florida football injury update | Two QBs listed as questionable for Georgia Kevin Brockway Gainesville Sun Updated Oct. 28, 2026, 8:56 p.m. ET Florida football made its quarterback situation even more cloudy heading into its matchup against rival Georgia in Atlanta. The top two Florida Gators quarterbacks on the depth chart − Aaron Philio and Tramell Jones Jr.−are both listed as questionable for UF's showdown with the Bulldogs. Philo, who started UF's first six games for the Gators , sat out Florida 's game against Texas on October 17 with a shoulder injury. Jones, who led UF to an upset win over the Longhorns by passing for 155 yards and 2 TDs, is dealing with an undisclosed injury. "He’s got a couple of bumps and bruises, too, now," Sumrall said. "And he had, you know, pulled the guy fresh out of that garage and he goes and plays, and he got a couple fender-benders. So, there's some bumps and bruises he's dealing with that are new. I noticed it last week." Also on the availability report, inside linebacker Jaden Robinson and wide receiver Bailey Stockton are listed as doubtful for UF, while running back Duke Clark has been upgraded to questionable. Wide receiver Vernell Brown III, who has missed UF's last three games with a knee strain, is listed as probable. For Georgia, wide receiver Thomas Blackshear, outside linebacker Amaris Williams and safety Tyriq Green have been ruled out. Preseason All-SEC safety KJ Bolden is listed as questionable, along with running back Chauncey Bowens and wide receiver Isiah Canon. Florida coach Jon Sumrall said both practiced this week and hinted Jones was dealing with issues following the Texas win during his opening week press conference on October 26. If Jones and Philo both can't go, Florida would turn to its third-string quarterback, redshirt junior Aidan Warner, or true freshman Will Griffin. Warner appeared in the Florida-Georgia game in 2024 when DJ Lagway went down with a hamstring injury and made one career start the following week at Texas. No. 20 Florida (5-2. 3-2 SEC) is looking to break five-game losing streak against the Bulldogs (6-1, 4-1 SEC) when the two schools meet on Saturday, October 31 (3:30 p.m., ABC). The game, traditionally held in Jacksonville, was moved to Mercedes-Benz Stadium in Atlanta due to the $1.4 billion renovation at EverBank Stadium for the NFL's Jacksonville Jaguars. picks.headline: Previewing Northwestern's Upcoming Matchup Against Oregon as They Prepare to Face Another Tough Test on the Road
picks.blurb: Previewing Northwestern's Upcoming Matchup Against Oregon as They Prepare to Face Another Tough Test on the Road Skip to main content SI.COM Olympic Sports More from Northwestern Wildcats On SI FOOTBALL The Wildcats hit the road once again, this time traveling west to Eugene, Oregon, for a Big Ten showdown against the Oregon Ducks on Saturday at 2:30 p.m. CT. Oregon enters Saturday’s matchup looking to bounce back following a 21-10 loss to Illinois. The Ducks have been without starting quarterback Dante Moore for the past three games, and recent reports indicate he is unlikely to return this season after suffering a concussion earlier this year against USC. Oregon now sits at 10th in the conference with a 4-3 overall record this season. Meanwhile, the Wildcats enter Saturday’s matchup fresh off a commanding 42-14 home victory over Rutgers, a win that propelled Northwestern to No. 20 in the AP Poll. A familiar face will return to Eugene this weekend, as former Oregon head coach Chip Kelly will take on the Ducks, this time as the Wildcats’ offensive coordinator. Under Kelly’s leadership, Northwestern’s offense has emerged as one of the best in the Big Ten this season, ranking third in the conference in total yards and points per game and second in rushing yards per game. The Wildcats head to Eugene looking to build on their success on both sides of the ball and extend their four-game winning streak. A major contributor to Northwestern’s offensive success this season has been quarterback Aidan Chiles, this week’s Big Ten Offensive Player of the Week, who has thrown for over 1,600 yards and 12 touchdowns, while recording just one interception. Chiles was dominant last time out against Rutgers, throwing for 219 yards and passing for three touchdowns, while rushing for 83 yards and two touchdowns. Oct 24, 2026; Evanston, Illinois, USA; Northwestern Wildcats quarterback Aidan Chiles (0) runs with the ball against the Rutgers Scarlet Knights during the first half at New Ryan Field. Credit: David Banks- | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Alongside Chiles, wide receiver Griffin Wilde has been another standout for David Braun’s squad, recording 39 receptions for 615 yards and four touchdowns this season. Alongside Chiles, wide receiver Griffin Wilde has been another standout for David Braun’s squad, recording 39 receptions for 615 yards and four touchdowns this season. Northwestern’s rushing attack has also been a major part of its offensive success, led by the dynamic running back duo of Caleb Komolafe and Joseph Himon II, who have combined for over 900 rushing yards this season. Komolafe delivered an especially impressive performance against Rutgers, rushing for 150 yards and a touchdown in the Wildcats’ convincing victory. Defensively, Northwestern has remained stout this season, spearheaded by defensive back Robert Fitzgerald and line backer Braydon Brus. Despite missing the last two games due to injury, Fitzgerald has recorded 49 tackles and two interceptions this season. The defensive back leads the Big Ten in tackles per game with nine, followed closely by Brus in second with 8.9. Brus leads the defensive unit with 62 tackles and has also notched an interception and fumble recovery this season. Despite Dante Moore’s potential absence the rest of the season, Northwestern will still face a tough challenge on the road against a talented Oregon team. Quarterbacks Dylan Raiola and Brock Thomas have shared playing time the past three games for the Ducks. Raiola struggled in last weekend’s loss to Illinois, completing 27 of 41 passes for 246 yards, as the defeat dealt a major blow to Oregon’s hopes of reaching the College Football Playoff for a third consecutive season. This weekend’s matchup will be just the third time that both teams will be meeting, and the first time that they will match up at Autzen Stadium. picks.blurb: What time, TV channel is Oregon vs. Northwestern? Game preview, prediction, betting line - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football College Football Playoff NFL injury tracker Belichick-Hudson breakup Brewers' championship parade Chet Holmgren injury Fantasy Start 'Em, Sit 'Em Ryan Clarke Fri, October 30, 2026 at 3:29 PM UTC · 4 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Seeking to climb out of the low point of its 2026 season, Oregon football returns home on Halloween to host No. 20 Northwestern. Legendary Oregon coach Chip Kelly is calling plays on the opposite sideline as the Wildcats' offensive coordinator, and Dan Lanning will rely on interim play-caller Jay Johnson to run his offense following the firing of Drew Mehringer. Can the Ducks get their minds right and put together a convincing performance on both sides of the ball for a win over a ranked team? Here is a full preview: Oregon (4-3, 2-2 Big Ten) vs. No. 20 Northwestern (6-1, 3-1) When: Saturday, Oct. 31 Time: 12:30 p.m. PT Where: Autzen Stadium, Eugene Latest line: Oregon by 3.5 points Radio: Oregon Sports Network Stream : You can watch this game streaming only on Peacock (costs just $12.99/month). There is no traditional cable TV broadcast for this game as it is one of several Peacock-exclusive Big Ten football matchups that will appear on NBC's streaming platform. Streaming broadcasts for this game will be available on these streaming services locally in Oregon and Washington, but may not be available outside of the Pacific Northwest, depending on your location. A RUNNING THREAT Northwestern quarterback Aidan Chiles has been to Autzen Stadium before. The former Oregon State and Michigan State signal-caller is having a career year, completing 71.3% of his passes for 1,617 yards, 12 touchdowns and one interception. Chiles is also a serious threat with his legs, rushing for nine touchdowns this season. That versatility could cause the Oregon defense problems, particularly with how creative Kelly is getting with the Northwestern offense. The Ducks' game plan starts and ends with getting pressure on Chiles and keeping him contained in the run game as well. The Wildcats are No. 35 in the country at 34.7 points per game. For all the dominance Oregon's defense has shown despite the struggles of its offense, this Northwestern team has the best and most balanced offense of any team the Ducks have faced these past four weeks. Oregon's quarterback situation remains up in the air after another poor performance from Dylan Raiola against Illinois. While the Nebraska transfer has had his moments this season, his play in two losses to UCLA and Illinois raises serious cause for concern. Enter sophomore Akili Smith Jr., the son of the former Oregon quarterback, who some fans are clamoring for to start this week. He has a big arm and all the physical traits one could want at the position, but is he ready to face a fearsome Northwestern defense? The answer to that question will determine whether Lanning and company decide to hand the keys to Oregon's flailing offense over to Smith. If the Ducks still think they are better off with a veteran presence in Raiola, despite his struggles, that will delay Smith's starting debut. But it's hard to imagine Oregon's quarterback play being any worse, so, why not give it a shot? GETTING PLAYMAKERS BACK Oregon should have three of its top wide receivers back against Northwestern who missed the Illinois game: Evan Stewart, Messiah Hampton and Jalen Lott. Stewart was dealing with an injury that kept him out of the Nebraska game, after which he was arrested on suspicion of DUII. And the reason for Hampton and Lott's absence on the trip to Champaign is unknown, though Lanning did not note any specific injury. Whoever starts at quarterback for Oregon will benefit from a full complement of receivers, save for the injured Jeremiah McClellan. Northwestern gets a crucial player back this week, too: tight end Luke Dehnicke no longer appears on the injury report. He had a massive performance last time he took the field against Indiana on Sept. 25, hauling in seven passes for 140 yards. A lot of the things that we ask our players to do are things I don't think grown men do well, right? When it's good, there's a level of energy and effort. When it's not good, it almost looks like your dog died. You just can't operate that way in our profession, in the job we do. You've got to bring it every single play." —Oregon coach Dan Lanning SERIES HISTORY The all-time series is tied, 1-1.
