(Photo by Zoe Davis/Getty Images) | Getty Images Inside NU Archives Fri, October 30, 2026 at 11:40 PM UTC · 10 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Northwestern has played itself into College Football Playoff contention. The 'Cats sit as the No. 20-ranked team in the nation, with six wins over South Dakota State, Colorado, Penn State, Michigan State, Ball State and Rutgers, and a narrow 29-23 loss on the road to the now No. 4-ranked Indiana Hoosiers. Thus far this season, they've passed the eye test, wowing pundits around the country with creative offensive formations and a turnover happy defense, but they are in need of quality wins over top-notch opponents. Over the next four weeks, NU will get three chances to secure resumé-changing victories, with matchups booked against Oregon, Iowa, Ohio State and Minnesota. The first of which, against Dan Lanning's Ducks, will take place on Saturday. Here's the INU staff's predictions for the 'Cats' road test against the 4-3 Oregon Ducks: Charlie Jacobs (27-16 Northwestern ) This Northwestern team has a different vibe to it. Although the Wildcats' last road trip was too close for comfort, Oregon has been struggling a lot lately and offers the perfect opportunity for Northwestern to pick up the win. Whether it's Brock Thomas or Dylan Raiola at quarterback, I'm not sure the Ducks can keep up with the Wildcats' offense, which will likely score enough no matter what. Plus, Chip Kelly back calling plays in Autzen… there's very few storylines better than that this week. Oregon, while a very talented roster, hasn't been able to put it all together. Even with a new offensive coordinator this week (or lack thereof), Oregon's offense has to prove it can compete for it to be threatening, even if the weapons are healthy. I'm taking the 'Cats. Jackson Pick (24-13 Northwestern ) Northwestern enters the meat of its schedule on a four-game winning streak, and at face value it's hard not to favor the 'Cats here. Aidan Chiles collected five total touchdowns against Rutgers on Saturday, with Caleb Komolafe adding one of his own to go with his 150 rushing yards on the day. Oregon, one of the preseason national championship favorites, has lost two of its last three, including a 21-10 shocker at Illinois that knocked it out of College Football Playoff contention. One reason for the Ducks' slide is obvious: their quarterback and potential No. 1-overall pick Dante Moore suffered a head injury against USC, and neither Dylan Raiola nor Brock Thomas have been able to sufficiently replace his production — Oregon has gone from 304 passing yards per game to just 205 since Moore's injury. On Saturday, Moore's continued absence will once again stifle an Oregon offense whose rushing attack hasn't produced enough to supplement its weakened passing game. While its defense has been stout enough, Northwestern will travel to Eugene with the strongest offense the Ducks have faced since their Week 2 loss to Oklahoma State. This game – if the Wildcats can win it – will begin to put the CFP in their sights. Autzen Stadium is a raucous environment to travel to for a NU team that's struggled on the road, and this is easily their biggest test since traveling to face Indiana. Unlike with the Hoosiers, though, the 'Cats don't need to execute at 100% to take this one. On another big day for the Wildcats' defense, Chiles will do just enough to escape Autzen with a season-defining victory. Donovan West (21-17 Oregon ) Five punts, three missed field goals and a fumble. That's how eight of Oregon's drives ended against Illinois last week. It was a masterclass in miscues from head coach Dan Lanning and the Ducks in a disappointing result that marked a season that has spun out of control. Despite a roster made up mostly of four- and five-star recruits, Oregon is 4-3 and has proven that raw talent doesn't automatically make a good football team. Northwestern, however, has proven the opposite. The 'Cats are an injury-ridden team of misfits that has united around a common goal and beaten the breaks off of three power conference teams. The only problem for NU is that its dominance has made the games boring to watch and has led to the Wildcat Wall leaving early.​ Yet, with the two programs on opposite trajectories, Oregon will still walk onto its home field on Saturday as favorites. The sports books trust the Ducks' depth and talent, and so do I. Their victories over USC and Nebraska, two wins more impressive than anything Northwestern has done, show that Oregon can still be a good football team. The Ducks will trot into Autzen Stadium knowing they need to win for any chance at making the playoff and grind their way to victory with a dominant performance in the trenches. As it did against Indiana, Northwestern will struggle to run the ball against Oregon, and Aidan Chiles won't be able to get it done through the air. The 'Cats' dreamy season will take a reality check, and expectations will be reevaluated. Zac Penson (24-17 Oregon ) I want to be wrong. The biggest hump I struggle to get over is that Oregon still has a stellar defense. Despite losing Dante Moore for the year, their experience and poise on defense is something they have continued to show over the past few weeks, allowing only 17 points to UCLA and just 14 points to Nebraska. Northwestern has also seemed to struggle on the road this season, falling to Indiana and squeaking out a win over Michigan State. And this stadium will be louder. Coming in at No. 20 on the AP Poll against an unranked Oregon team, the Wildcats have something to prove. Oregon lost to Illinois last week, so they clearly aren't invincible, but that was in Champaign. Autzen Stadium is a whole different animal. Despite losing to Illinois, Oregon is indeed favored. I would love to see the Cardiac 'Cats pull off the upset on this one, but I believe the pressure of the moment is only mounting for the Wildcats as the days drag on and they board their flight to Eugene. I believe Northwestern won't go down without a fight, though, and I expect this one to be a fun battle to the end. Whitley Williams (24-21 Northwestern ) Blurb: Strike while the opponent is weak. Northwestern is seeking its fifth consecutive win against the Oregon Ducks. Once considered a College Football Playoff contender, Oregon has endured a series of unexpected setbacks. The Ducks fired offensive coordinator Drew Mehringer following their loss to Illinois. Once known for their explosive offense and "Pac-12 After Dark" spectacles, the Ducks are now a team searching for their identity. In many ways, the roles have reversed. Northwestern boasts a creative, explosive offense that keeps opposing defenses guessing. Offensive coordinator Chip Kelly will need to lean on that trickery against an elite Oregon defense that allows just 3.65 yards per carry and 197.6 passing yards a game. Assistant quarterbacks coach Jay Johnson will call the plays for Oregon on Saturday. With Dante Moore out for the season, Oregon will start Dylan Raiola at quarterback. Against Illinois, Raiola completed 66% of his passes for 246 yards but couldn't finish the job. The Wildcats will have to lock down deep-threat wide receiver Dakorien Moore. Aidan Chiles has played extremely tough on the road in hostile environments, and this test in Eugene will certainly show what the Wildcats are truly made of. Kussh Mital (21-10 Northwestern ) I don't see why this game should be any different than Oregon's previous matchup against Illinois. I believe this so much that I am predicting that same score in the Wildcats favor. Oregon's defense is great, don't get me wrong, but they just gave up over 200 rushing yards to Illinois, and Northwestern has a flat out better rushing attack. Moreover, Northwestern can air the ball out much more efficiently, something the Ducks have not had to deal with in a couple weeks. Aidan Chiles is the best quarterback Oregon has faced since Jayden Maiava, who threw for over 300 yards and two touchdown passes against it. Chiles probably won't do that, but he will certainly do some damage. However, the main issue for this Oregon squad is the quarterback position. When you can't trust your quarterback to run the offense effectively, it's hard to expect to win the game. Even with the return of some of the receivers for Oregon, Dylan Raiola is not going to get the job done against Northwestern. With the Wildcats somehow entering the game as underdogs, I expect them to wear that title with honor and make Oregon fans extra fearful on Halloween. Drew Christmann (23-16 Northwestern ) Since Dante Moore went down with a scary and controversial injury against USC, Oregon has a simple problem: they can't score. Since that Week 4 matchup in LA, the Ducks have scored no more than 17 points a game, down from 47.5 in prior games, including an 84-0 shutout against Portland. Now, after firing offensive coordinator Drew Mehringer following a loss to Illinois last week, in which the Ducks scored just 10 points, it's unclear what Oregon's offense will look like going forward, with Dan Lanning confirming he doesn't expect Moore to return for the rest of the season. Northwestern is the opposite. After years of a less-than-optimal offense, the Wildcats have been one of the conference's best, especially on the ground, where they average 204.6 yards per game. Aidan Chiles has been no slouch in the air, too, throwing for 1,617 yards with a 71.3% completion rate and just one interception. That, along with Chip Kelly's return to Autzen, makes for a scary matchup for Oregon. The ideal situation for the 'Cats' is a quick start, as it did against Rutgers last week, when they scored on the first three possessions of the game. But Northwestern has shown they know how to play from behind in hostile environments, like in Bloomington, where they scored 16 points in the final quarter to push defending champion Indiana Hoosiers to the brink and at Michigan State in East Lansing, where Chiles drove 64 yards against his former school to win on a game-winning kick. The Wildcats have shown they can win both ways, and against an Oregon team whose season is spiraling, I see Northwestern moving to 7-1 on Halloween. Adam Sutro (27-24 Northwestern ) I have low confidence in Northwestern's defense entering this football game. A poor Rutgers offense killed the 'Cats on the ground last week, exposing a run defense issue that has been a problem all year for Northwestern. Fortunately for the 'Cats, Oregon has operated more through the air than on the ground for most of the season… though I think with all the talent the Ducks have on their offensive line, they will figure out how to expose the 'Cats' run defense and move the ball. However, this 'Cats defense is also one that can capitalize on mistakes and Oregon's offense has made a LOT of mistakes this year. In fact, Northwestern ranks No. 6

picks.headline: Ducks Wire staff predicts Oregon Ducks vs. Northwestern Wildcats
picks.blurb: That seems like a long time ago, doesn't it? Less than a week later, we are sitting with the Ducks at 4-3, having just fired offensive coordinator Drew Mehringer following another loss, and quarterback Dante Moore announcing that his 2026 season is over after the concussion he suffered earlier this year against USC. Now, with a laundry list of questions to answer, the Ducks go forward into a brutal home matchup against the No. 20 Northwestern Wildcats , hoping that they can somehow manage to get back to their winning ways. To preview the game, we go through our weekly roundtable with the writers from Ducks Wire to offer our opinions and predictions for what's to come. Here is our roundtable conversation. Question: Well, it's certainly been an eventful week in Eugene. Let's start with the biggest news: Dante Moore is not expected to play again this season. With the Ducks sitting at 4-3 and their playoff hopes essentially gone, what are your expectations for the rest of the season? What would a successful finish look like? Zachary Neel: At this point, a successful season is going 7-5 on the year and making it to a semi-respectable bowl game when all is said and done, and that's incredibly sad to say, considering where this season started. Just about everything has gone wrong for Oregon thus far, and I truly do see a reality where they struggle to even become bowl-eligible. But I think the culture wins out, and Dan Lanning can rally this team over the final five weeks. Bjorn Bergstrom: The culture that we’ve come to know in recent seasons is of a team that stays together and fights, no matter the circumstances. That hasn’t been the case in 2026, but if they can reclaim that fight and grittiness, then I think that should be considered a success. The way things are going, it’s hard to stamp “success” on a certain win total. It’s more about the process and the eye test, rather than the end result. Logan Brown: It’s hard to find any success in this season at this point. I guess if Oregon beats Washington, that’s probably the least you could ask for? I would say an 8-4 finish would mean the Ducks played well in November and finished strong, but that probably means losses to Northwestern and Ohio State. It’s probably going to get worse before it gets any better. Drew Mehringer Question: Dan Lanning made one of the biggest decisions of his coaching career on Sunday, firing offensive coordinator Drew Mehringer after Oregon's loss to Illinois. Do you agree with the decision, and how much of the blame for Oregon's offensive struggles falls on Mehringer compared to the players and other coaches? Zachary Neel: I think a change needed to be made, but I also don't think this change is going to lead to a switch being flipped for the Oregon offense. The problems go much deeper than just the play calling, in my opinion, and I don't think we're going to all of a sudden see the Ducks putting up 27-31 points per game because Mehringer is no longer in the building. As the OC, he was rightfully the guy to fall on the sword, but more changes are needed this offseason. Bjorn Bergstrom: It's hard not to agree with the decision. Fans had been on him from the very beginning, it seemed, but I was finally on board after last week’s debacle. As far as the blame, there’s some that goes to the position coaches who didn’t have their guys ready to play individually, but the play calls were what stuck out to me in particular. It didn’t seem like Mehringer had the ability to scheme up easy looks for his quarterbacks and easy running holes for his backs. There was a clear lack of creativity. Just watch any other top-25 team in college football and you’ll see the difference in outside-of-the-box thinking schematically that Mehringer just couldn’t manage to implement. Logan Brown: Unfortunately, I do feel like it was the right move. There were so many times where it just seemed like the offense was lacking situational awareness because of the play call. I lost count of the amount of times the Ducks ran a third down play, from any distance, where receivers were all running routes short of the sticks. There were zero aggressive calls, and more aiming and carefully crafting open receivers to the point where if the defense had an answer, there was no counter. I do think Oregon’s lack of offensive line and quarterback development has played a significant role in the offense’s struggles, but Mehringer was a clear issue that the Ducks could do something about midseason. New Play-Caller Question: Jay Johnson is taking over play-calling duties for the Ducks, and he'll have quite the challenge trying to turn this offense around. What's the biggest change you hope to see from Oregon's offense under Johnson? And realistically, how much improvement can we expect in just one week? Zachary Neel: Asking Johnson to come in and completely change this offense is unfair and unrealistic. I think at the best, you can hope that Oregon's offensive scheme looks more simplified, leaning more heavily on running between the tackles, finding a rhythm, and getting the ball past the sticks on down-and-distance situations. But as far as an entirely new scheme that looks different from what we've seen over the past seven weeks, I'm not expecting that. Bjorn Bergstrom: The biggest thing I’ll be wanting to see is more creativity in the passing game as far as Dylan Raiola’s platform, whether it be rolling him out, sprint-outs, or moving the pocket so it’s not a straight dropback. Moving the quarterback in the backfield makes it so much more difficult for a defense to pinpoint where he’ll be on a given play, opening up the run game at the same time as they’ll be just a step slower. Also, no more Wildcat. Yuck. Logan Brown: Take some chances! Oregon has nothing to lose at this point. The Ducks have Ferraris all over the offense, but most throws are horizontal or short of the sticks. Safeties play close to the line because the Ducks don’t trust their quarterback to air it out. At this point, the season is gone, so why not air it out? Why not run more counters and try to produce explosive plays on the ground? I don't think Johnson changes a ton in just one week, but I do think he could set the tone with a different plan on critical downs. Question: Northwestern comes to Eugene at 6-1, ranked No. 20 in the nation, with former Oregon head coach Chip Kelly running the offense. The Wildcats have been one of the biggest surprises in the Big Ten this season. What concerns you most about this matchup, and where do you think Northwestern has the biggest advantage over Oregon? Zachary Neel: Any time Oregon faces a true dual-threat quarterback who can beat you with his feet, Duck fans get worried. That has been the Achilles heel in Eugene for years, and Aidan Chiles is as good at that as anyone. With his ability both in the air and on the ground, plus Chip Kelly's offensive mind, I know that the Ducks' defense is going to have its hands full on Saturday. Bjorn Bergstrom: I think that Northwestern has a simple, yet very important advantage: they play sound, complementary football much, much better than the Ducks have this season. They’ve been a complete team, complimenting each other on offense, defense and special teams and picking up for the other when needed. That’s something Oregon hasn’t done this season, and I don’t expect them to on Saturday. Logan Brown: I’m so interested in this battle of the ground with Northwestern’s run game. They have a three-headed monster in the backfield, plus the mobility of quarterback Aidan Chiles. The Wildcats have run the ball so well this season, but it hasn’t always come easy on the road. Oregon has played the run better the past few weeks, but the Ducks couldn’t stop Illinois on the ground in the second half last week. If Northwestern runs the ball efficiently, they win with a huge advantage. If not, it can get interesting. Question: We've talked a lot about Oregon's offensive struggles, but the defense will have its hands full with Chip Kelly and a Northwestern offense that's been rolling this season. What's the biggest key for Oregon's defense to slow down the Wildcats and give the Ducks a chance to win? Zachary Neel: As I mentioned above, it's going to be all about slowing down the run for Northwestern. That means more than just Chiles, though. The Wildcats have a trio of very good running backs that can hurt you in different ways. If Northwestern is able to find success on the ground, it will open up the play-action passing game, where tight end Luke Dehnicke can be lethal. Bjorn Bergstrom: The biggest key is forcing Aidan Chiles to have an off day and revert back to his struggles from his first three seasons. During that time, Chiles was an erratic, turnover-prone passer lacking confidence. In 2026, he’s full of confidence and is an absolute baller, making plays that simply weren’t imaginable just 12 months ago. Getting in his face, making him feel pressure and not be able to get going with easy throws early is imperative for the Ducks. But with Kelly’s scheme, I lean towards Chiles being able to get going early. Logan Brown: I already talked about the run game, but the Ducks need to play disciplined against Chiles. The senior quarterback can burn them with RPO plays or just a regular read option. Northwestern utilizes the whole field with wide splits, so the pressure is on Oregon’s edge rushers more than ever to contain Chiles in the option and quick game and avoid getting caught too far up field. Gambling Corner Question: Gambling Corner: You get $100 to spread across the point spread (Oregon -3.5), and the Over/Under (47.5 points). How are you allocating your funds? Zachary Neel: Give me all $100 on Northwestern to cover. Vegas always knows something, but I don't know what in the world they've seen from the Ducks over the past month to consider them a 3.5-point favorite here. Bjorn Bergstrom: I think Northwestern will win, so I’m tempted to go there, but what in the world is pulling the over/under so high? Mehringer is gone but the bones of the offense are still here, along with a Ducks defense that has been dominant. I don’t see either team surpassing 24 points, so I’ll put all $100 on the under. What will be the final result? The Oregon Ducks and Northwestern Wildcats enter Saturday’s matchup with very different expectations than they had at the beginning of the season. Oregon was expected to compete for a College Football Playoff spot, but a disappointing season, quarterback Dante Moore’s season-ending injury, and offensive coaching changes have left the Ducks searching for answers. Northwestern, meanwhile, has emerged as one of the biggest surprises in college football, entering the matchup at 6-1 and looking to strengthen its postseason resume. Can the Wildcats take advantage of Oregon’s struggles and leave Autzen Stadium with a statement victory? Or will the Ducks’ talent advantage be enough to get them back on track? Here is how the A to Z Sports team sees Saturday’s game playing out. A to Z Sports Score Predictions Tyler Forness — A to Z Sports Florida Prediction: Northwestern 24, Oregon 14 Going into the season, projecting the Wildcats to beat the Ducks would have been a shocker. On Halloween, it won’t be a trick, but rather a Wildcat treat. What Chip Kelly has done with this offense and head coach David Braun overall has been very impressive. They aren’t just 6-1 overall this season, but rank seventh in adjusted EPA/play on offense. It’s been a wild turnaround, and even though the Ducks have a huge talent surplus, their coaching staff is not in a great place, and Dante Moore is out for the year. The Northwestern playoff push continues on after a big win Saturday. Rob Gregson — A to Z Sports Alabama Prediction: Northwestern 25, Oregon 20 The 2026 Oregon Ducks are a case study in why turnover at the coordinator positions is problematic. That, and why if you can go to the NFL and be a high first-rounder, you should. The loss of Dante Moore for the season underscores what has been a messy situation from start to finish on offense this season. Will Stein has the Wildcats thriving in Kentucky, and that loss is felt in a major way. But the defense hasn’t been much better. Now, a Northwestern squad that is willing to run the ball at will is heading to Oregon, and I think they will challenge the physicality of the Ducks in a major way. Oregon doesn’t have the firepower to score, and it will be a massive win for Northwestern. Craig Smith — A to Z Sports Miami Prediction: Northwestern 23, Oregon 19 Boy, how the perception of this game has changed since Labor Day weekend. Oregon’s playoff goose is cooked at 4-3 after losses to Oklahoma State, UCLA, and Illinois. Dante Moore is done for the season. Offensive coordinator Drew Mehringer was fired after the loss to the Illini. In other words, things are a mess, particularly on the offensive side of the ball. This one stays close at Autzen Stadium, as the Ducks move the ball relatively well early on. But Northwestern, while allowing 364.6 yards per game, has been very good at keeping the point total lower, ranking 22nd nationally at 16.6 points per game. The Wildcats force some early field goals, and their ground game, paced by Caleb Komolafe, takes over the second half as the Wildcats get out of town at 7-1 and firmly in the Big Ten and playoff races. Justin Churchill — A to Z Sports Oklahoma Prediction: Oregon 20, Northwestern 17 Oregon is favored in this matchup currently by a field goal. And I have them winning by just that. Northwestern is a good team, and their story is amazing. But I think Oregon’s overall talent and coaching advantage in this one is just too good. Northwestern does have a +9 turnover margin. They force them, and they don’t commit them. Oregon cannot say the same. They have also scored on 96% of their red zone opportunities this year, which is extremely good. So, I can see why that would be enticing. But this Oregon roster is just too talented to give up on yet. Ryan Roberts — A to Z Sports Notre Dame Prediction: Oregon 21, Northwestern 20 Northwestern has earned plenty of respect with its performance this season, but I’m still leaning toward Oregon to find a way to win at home. The Ducks have endured a difficult stretch, and losing Dante Moore for the season makes an already challenging situation even more complicated. Still, the talent on this roster is difficult to overlook, particularly in a game that could come down to one or two critical possessions. Northwestern’s ability to run the football and protect the ball makes the Wildcats a dangerous opponent, especially against an Oregon team that has struggled to find consistency. However, I expect the Ducks to make just enough plays offensively to survive a tight finish. Northwestern has a legitimate opportunity to pull off the upset, but I’m giving Oregon the narrow edge at Autzen Stadium. Consensus: Can Northwestern Finish the Upset? The A to Z Sports predictions lean heavily toward Northwestern, with four of the five analysts picking the Wildcats to win. The common theme is Oregon’s offensive instability following Dante Moore’s season-ending injury and the coaching changes that have contributed to an uneven campaign. Northwestern’s ability to run the football, limit opponents’ scoring, and capitalize on mistakes gives the Wildcats a path to a major road victory. Justin Churchill and I are the exceptions, backing Oregon to lean on its roster talent and home-field advantage. Both expect a close game, and I am predicting a one-point Ducks victory. Regardless of the final score, Northwestern has an opportunity to turn an impressive start into a season-defining result. Oregon, meanwhile, needs to show that its talent can overcome the problems that have derailed its season. If the Wildcats establish the run and force Oregon into uncomfortable passing situations, an upset in Eugene could be very much in play. What happened instead raises questions about Dan Lanning's program that go beyond one bad game. Over the past few weeks, Moore had returned to practice for Oregon, participating with the team on a daily basis. But, in terms of returning to the field in an uncontrolled environment, Dan Lanning mentioned that he can not be cleared by the Ducks medical team for a return to live action. "Really got clarity for us over the past week. I think if it was up to Dante in any shape or way, he would want to be out there playing for the guys," Lanning said on Monday. "But unfortunately, it's not really up to Dante, and it's not really up to me. We can control the settting of practice where he's able to do things for us, where that's not always the case in a game. "You know, we said before that this is a serious deal that he'll 100% be able to make a full recovery from. That has not changed, I definitely feel that way. But for him to be out there on the field for us right now, that's not going to happen." "We're getting one of the best scout team looks in practice every week, and he looks good out there," Lanning mentioned. "This isn’t like a selfish decision on Dante's part saying 'I don't wanna come back, the season doesn’t look like theyw ay I want it to look'. That's not at all what this is." The Gamecocks' success is primarily due to their rushing offense that averages an SEC-best 218.3 yards per game. It's been a combination of running back Matt Fuller and quarterback LaNorris Sellers on the ground. Fuller has 513 yards and five touchdowns. Sellers is right behind him with 507 yards and four touchdowns. The Sooners' offense is bogged down by its SEC-worst run game, but the passing game has also had its ups and downs. John Mateer has thrown for 1,591 yards at a 66.7% completion rate with 11 touchdowns to seven interceptions, tied for the second most in the SEC. Wide receiver Isaiah Sategna III has the sixth-most receiving yards in the SEC with 578 and three touchdowns Although the Sooners have faced plenty of challenges offensively, their defense has played well, ranking second in the SEC in total yards allowed and first in pass defense. Part of their ability to defend well against the pass is their pass rush that's gotten 22 sacks, which ties for third in the SEC. South Carolina vs Oklahoma scouting report Why South Carolina has an advantage: Even though Oklahoma's defense is its strength, against the run, the Sooners haven't been as formidable as they are against the pass. They allow an average of 117.4 rushing yards, ranking eighth in the SEC. This favors a South Carolina team that gains most of its yards on the ground. As for facing the Sooners' pressure on passing plays, the Gamecocks' offensive line has held its own, allowing 15 sacks, tied for sixth in the SEC. Sellers' mobility will also be an asset in allowing him to escape the pocket and break free on scrambles, in addition to his designed runs. Why Oklahoma has an advantage: The Sooners have struggled to score but now face a bottom-five SEC defense in points allowed. Mateer could have an easier time settling into a rhythm against the Gamecocks, who give up 222.7 passing yards per game and have just four interceptions. picks.headline: Staff Picks: Can Oklahoma Build on Last Week's Success Against South Carolina?
picks.blurb: Staff Picks: Can Oklahoma Build on Last Week's Success Against South Carolina? - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football College Football Playoff NFL injury tracker Belichick-Hudson breakup Brewers' championship parade Chet Holmgren injury Fantasy Start 'Em, Sit 'Em Oklahoma quarterback John Mateer scans the defense before a snap against MSU. | Carson Field / Sooners On SI Ryan Chapman Fri, October 30, 2026 at 2:00 PM UTC · 4 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads It's going to be much harder to run the football this week against a stout South Carolina defense. If the Sooners can continue their upward trajectory against the Gamecocks, they'll have a chance. If not - if John Mateer has to lead the team in rushing attempts and the Sooners average less than 4 yards per carry, then desperation will set in, Mateer will be forced to make plays - then bad things will happen. But if OU can run the ball just a little, Mateer can relax and guys like Isaiah Sategna and Rocky Beers and Lloyd Avant can help out the defense by moving the chains, changing the scoreboard and winning a home game. Final: Oklahoma 21, South Carolina 13 John Mateer found a healthy headspace in Starkville, but Saturday will be the first real test to see if he can stick to the plan. South Carolina's defense is not impenetrable, but it's a much better group than Mississippi State's, with difference-makers who can wreck drives and put Mateer into tough situations. It's likely there will be a turnover, and the test will be if OU's quarterback can rebound after that. History says he'll have a tough time. Brent Venables' defense will get its third look at talented quarterback LaNorris Sellers, but if Oklahoma is unable to finish off drives, the Gamecocks have shown they can notch dramatic victories. Final: South Carolina 20, Oklahoma 13 Someone from the future could tell me a plethora of different outcomes from Saturday's game, and I'd believe them. Oklahoma's offense certainly made progress against Mississippi State, and it's possible that the Sooners build on those improvements at home against South Carolina. But it also wouldn't be shocking if OU's offense regressed into the turnover-prone unit that it was against Kentucky, Georgia, New Mexico and Michigan. South Carolina comes into Norman on a two-game winning streak after ranked victories over Florida (on the road) and Tennessee - the Gamecocks seem like they're due for a letdown. While South Carolina's defense is better than Mississippi State's was, there are plenty of areas for the Sooners to expose, assuming they can play a similarly clean game on Saturday. Oklahoma needs a win to stay above .500, and I expect the Sooners to earn a close victory over the Gamecocks. Final: Oklahoma 20, South Carolina 17 The Gamecocks are more dangerous than Mississippi State, on both sides of the ball. Last week was a small step forward for the Sooners' offense, nota giant leap. Oklahoma quarterback John Mateer isn't completely fixed just because he had a solid game against the Bulldogs. But with Michael Fasusi back on the offensive line, the Sooners' offense adds layers. They don't have to have every element working in order to be successful. What they do need to do, though, is protect the football and keep up their strong defensive play. This game will be back and forth and figures to go down to the wire, but in the end, Oklahoma does just enough to start its first winning streak of the season. Brady Trantham The 2026 season is still up in the air. One thing it has told us is that basically no one has been able to handle a big emotional win and follow that up with another win a week later. South Carolina's win over Tennessee was very much an emotional win against a highly-ranked opponent - the Volunteers themselves had just beaten Alabama the week prior. OU has slowly built consistency on offense, just enough that paired with an elite defense, victories against flawed teams are realistic. The Sooners have proven to be great at corralling mobile quarterbacks and will showcase that again, while John Mateer will build off a great performance last week against a dangerous but very gettable defense. The National Council on Problem Gambling help line is also often cited at 1-800-522-4700. Broadcast Details - TV: SEC Network and ESPN Unlimited (Taylor Zarzour, Gene Chizik and Michella Chester) - Radio: Sooner Sports Network via 107.7 The Franchise/KOKC 95.3 and 1520 in Oklahoma City, 1430 The Buzz/KMOD 97.5 in Tulsa, and on The Varsity Network app (Toby Rowland, Teddy Lehman, Chris Plank, and Gabe Ikard) What You Need To Know NORMAN, Okla. — Oklahoma's season has refused to settle into anything comfortable. Saturday's homecoming game against South Carolina is the next chance to stop the bouncing. The Sooners are 4-3 and 2-2 in the SEC heading into a 3:15 p.m. kickoff at Gaylord Family — Oklahoma Memorial Stadium. South Carolina arrives at 4-3 and 2-3, receiving votes, and playing with the confidence of a team that just knocked off Florida and Tennessee. That alone should wipe out any idea that this is a soft home date. The Gamecocks have already shown they can travel, finish close games, and lean on a quarterback who creates problems Oklahoma has to solve with discipline more than highlight-hunt pressure. There is history all over this one too. Shane Beamer spent 2018 through 2020 in Norman as Oklahoma's assistant head coach on offense, working tight ends and H-backs during a 33-6 stretch that included three Big 12 titles and two College Football Playoff appearances. Brent Venables, meanwhile, spent years tormenting South Carolina from the Clemson sideline. He went 7-2 against the Gamecocks as defensive coordinator and held them to 14.9 points per game in those seven wins. The recent series between these two programs has swung hard both ways: South Carolina won 35-9 in Norman in 2024 after Oklahoma turned it over on its first three possessions, then the Sooners answered with a 26-7 road win last year by smothering the Gamecocks and winning the line of scrimmage. That 2024 home loss is still the warning label. Oklahoma actually outgained South Carolina that day and held them to 69 second-half yards. It did not matter. Four turnovers and a 24-0 deficit in points off turnovers decided the afternoon before the Sooners ever found their footing. That has been the split-screen identity of this entire season too. In the wins over Texas and Mississippi State, Oklahoma had four takeaways and only one giveaway. In the losses to Georgia and Kentucky, it had two takeaways and eight giveaways. When the Sooners protect the ball, they look like a team that can still climb. When they do not, the defense gets asked to cover for a mess it did not create. The weirdest layer is the pattern. Oklahoma has followed every win with a loss and every loss with a win through seven games, the first time in program history the Sooners have alternated results across the first seven contests. If that pattern holds, homecoming would be a loss. That is exactly the kind of empty narrative this team needs to bury. South Carolina is the seventh straight opponent that was ranked or receiving votes at kickoff. The schedule has not given Oklahoma many clean emotional resets. This is another one that will have heat on it from the start. Oklahoma's defense remains the reason this team is still interesting. The Sooners lead the nation in first downs allowed per game and sit among the national leaders in third-down defense, red-zone defense, pass defense, sacks, and total defense. Opponents have scored on just 23 percent of their possessions. All 14 defensive starters began their college careers at Oklahoma. Owen Heinecke continues to lead the team in tackles and has become the week-to-week constant at linebacker. The front still has enough disruption to wreck drives when the edges stay clean. South Carolina's LaNorris Sellers is built to test that cleanliness. He is a big, physical quarterback who can push the ball downfield and punish soft contain with his legs. He has already thrown for more than 1,500 yards and added over 500 on the ground. The Gamecocks' recent upswing has come with far better ball security and enough confidence to finish against ranked teams. If Oklahoma's edge players get greedy or abandon lanes, Sellers can turn ordinary scrambles into drive-extending runs. The Sooners need a cage-rush approach more than a free-for-all. Squeeze the pocket, stay in assignment, and make him beat the structure with processing instead of freelancing into open space. Peyton Bowen's status adds some stress on the back end. He has been one of Oklahoma's most important defensive players all season, with takeaways that directly turned into points against Texas and Mississippi State. He is also coming out of the Mississippi State game dealing with a leg/stinger issue. If he is limited, somebody else has to clean up the explosive answers and help finish when Sellers extends plays. South Carolina's best chance is not a perfect 12-play drive script. It is one broken containment snap and one missed tackle in space. John Mateer's Starkville tape is the first real reset of the year at quarterback. He completed 22 of 29 passes for 283 yards and two touchdowns, did not throw an interception, and helped Oklahoma post season highs in total offense and rushing in a road win. Isaiah Sategna went off for 164 yards. Rocky Beers stayed productive. The run game finally had some weight to it, including a long run from Tory Blaylock that flipped the third quarter. Venables has already said that version of Mateer is what Oklahoma needs the rest of the way. That has to show up again Saturday. Mateer is at 1,591 passing yards, 11 touchdowns, and seven interceptions on the season. The efficiency can play. The turnover number is still the ceiling-cutter. South Carolina will give him enough looks to get comfortable if he stays patient and uses Beers as the safety valve while Sategna works the intermediate and deep parts of the field. Beers has been one of the better transfer additions in the league and continues to lead SEC tight ends in receiving yards per game. Sategna remains the explosive piece defenses have to account for every series. The offensive line remains the quieter concern. Availability has been uneven all season, and Oklahoma has had to patch together combinations on the fly. Against a South Carolina front that will try to clutter lanes and force Mateer into longer holds, that matters. The Sooners do not need 500 yards again. They need manageable downs, fewer empty possessions, and enough balance to keep Sellers' offense from owning the tempo of the day. There is a temptation to overstate every remaining game because the margin is already thin. Fair enough. ESPN's FPI has Oklahoma projected around the 6-6 range, and the remaining stretch still includes Florida, Ole Miss, Texas A&M, and Missouri. That means Saturday is not just another home date. It is one of the clearer opportunities to create breathing room. A win over South Carolina would make Oklahoma 5-3 and 3-2, with some actual traction in league play. It would also reinforce the only formula that has worked this year: defense travels, takeaways matter, and the quarterback has to stop donating points. A loss would push the Sooners back into the same uneasy place they occupied after Kentucky, with the season again asking whether the good nights are sustainable or just occasional interruptions. South Carolina is not an unknown. Beamer knows Norman. Sellers can take over a game if Oklahoma gets careless. The Gamecocks are playing better now than they were in September. All of that is true. It is also true that Oklahoma can win this game if it plays like the team that handled Texas and Mississippi State instead of the one that buried itself in turnovers against Georgia and Kentucky. Homecoming should not require a miracle. It requires cleanliness. Keep Sellers crowded. Make South Carolina drive the hard way. Let Mateer play the next snap instead of the last mistake. If the Sooners do that, Norman should still be a hard place to leave with a win. If they do not, the pattern everyone is already talking about will get one more chapter.

(Sam Wolfe/Special To The State) Michael Sauls Thu, October 29, 2026 at 11:00 AM UTC · 5 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads South Carolina football is hitting the road this weekend. Shane Beamer and the Gamecocks will travel to Norman, Oklahoma, on Saturday to face Brent Venables and the Oklahoma Sooners. The SEC matchup is set to kick off at 4:15 and will be televised on SEC Network. South Carolina (4-3, 2-3 SEC) is coming off a big win over then-No. 11 Tennessee last week. Oklahoma beat Mississippi State last week on the road. The Gamecocks and Sooners have played just twice in the all-time series. South Carolina beat Oklahoma on the road in 2024 and the Sooners beat the Gamecocks last year in Columbia. Here's what you need to know about Saturday's game: Is South Carolina vs. Oklahoma football game on TV? Who: South Carolina (4-3, 2-3 SEC) vs. Oklahoma (4-3, 2-3 SEC) When: Saturday, Oct. 31 at 4:15 p.m. Where : Memorial Stadium in Norman, Oklahoma Watch: SEC Network Stream: ESPN app or ESPN.com Broadcast crew: Taylor Zarzour, Gene Chizik, Michella Chester Local radio crew: Todd Ellis, Tommy Suggs, Chet Tucker Satellite radio: Sirius XM Channel 176 or 229 (953 on app) Series history: Tied 1-1 (Oklahoma won last matchup in 2025) South Carolina vs. Oklahoma betting odds Despite pulling off back-to-back ranked upsets, and being favored over then-No. 11 Tennessee last week, South Carolina is an underdog this week. Oklahoma opened as a 5.5-point favorite, according to the VegasInsider consensus . That line has since moved a bit and the Sooners are now favored by 4.5 points by major sportsbooks such as FanDuel and DraftKings. South Carolina is 3-4 against the spread this year. ESPN Analytics also favors the Sooners. ESPN gives South Carolina a 36.1% chance of winning the game. Injury updates South Carolina had seven players listed on the official SEC injury report released Wednesday night. WR Jayden Sellers, edge rusher Kobby Sakyi-Prah, OL Josian Thompson, OL Dayne Arnett and OL Seth Smith are all listed as out. Sellers and Thompson are both out for the year. DB Quay'sheed Scott and RB Jawarn Howell are both listed as doubtful. Scott has missed the last two games. Howell was out last week vs. Tennessee. The SEC injury report will be updated on Thursday, Friday and 90 minutes before kickoff on Saturday. Weather forecast for the game in Norman If you're making the trip to Oklahoma this weekend, be sure to pack an umbrella and a jacket. Temperatures aren't expected to surpass 64 degrees and will dip into the mid-50s. There will be thick cloud cover with a touch of rain, per Accuweather's 10-day forecast. There's a 55% chance of rain all day Saturday for the Norman area. Top storylines Three's a streak: A win over Oklahoma on Saturday would give South Carolina its third straight win. The Gamecocks haven't won three consecutive SEC games since they ended the 2024 season with four straight SEC wins. That six-game winning streak to close out the 2024 season was also the last time the Gamecocks won three games in a row. Should USC beat Oklahoma, it would get the Gamecocks' SEC record back to .500. Sellers needs help in the run game: Make no mistake, South Carolina still has the No. 1 rushing offense in the SEC. The Gamecocks are averaging 218 yards per game, but things haven't looked perfect in recent weeks. Anyone not named LaNorris Sellers has had trouble consistently running the ball for South Carolina. Sellers has accounted for 313 of the 480 rushing yards the Gamecocks have compiled in the last three games. That's certainly good, but USC's running backs need to get going so all the pressure isn't on Sellers' legs down the stretch. Ranking on the horizon? South Carolina received votes in both the Associated Press Top 25 and USA Today Coaches Poll this week after beating Tennessee. USC received 12 votes from the coaches and eight votes from the media. Will a win over Oklahoma be enough to catapult USC into the national rankings for the first time since September 2025? Only time will tell. South Carolina and Oklahoma players to watch South Carolina K Malik Orsan: The sophomore was South Carolina's savior last week. Orsan drilled a 48-yard field goal to help the Gamecocks beat then-No. 11 Tennessee 27-24 as the clock expired. The Southeast Missouri State transfer wasn't necessarily considered to be the top kicker on the roster during USC's kicking competition this offseason. But he's quickly proven why he won the starting job by going 10 for 12 on field goal attempts and 22 for 22 on extra-point attempts this season. South Carolina OL Nolan Hay: The fifth-year offensive lineman was named the Outland Trophy National Player of the Week on Tuesday by the Football Writers Association of America. Hay has been one of the best offensive linemen for the Gamecocks this year. He typically starts at guard but has played some center in Carter Miller's absence because of injury. Hay's Pro Football Focus blocking grade is one of the best on the team. Oklahoma QB John Mateer: There was some buzz around Mateer's name this offseason, but he's found himself in a bit of a rut in 2026. Mateer has thrown for 1,591 yards and 11 touchdowns but has also thrown seven interceptions. He's got a strong arm and is capable of using his legs in the ground game, but has been generally turnover-prone this season. Oklahoma WR Isaiah Sategna III: Sategna was an All-SEC player last year after finishing with 965 receiving yards. The fifth-year student has been Mateer's favorite target in 2026. Sategna leads Oklahoma with 41 catches and 578 yards.

away.headline: Oklahoma vs. South Carolina: Initial injury report for Week 9
away.blurb: On offense, key players Ryan Fodje and Eddy Pierre-Louis aren't close to returning and were ruled out. However, guard Heath Ozaeta could make his first appearance since the win over Texas. Ozaeta was listed as probable. If he's able to play, he provides Oklahoma a valuable piece to its interior offensive line rotation. If he's able to play, it's likely Ozaeta slides back into the starting lineup, though he could platoon with Peyton Joseph, who has had ups and downs for the Sooners the last two weeks. It also looks like running back Xavier Robinson could be available this week. The Carl Albert High School graduate hasn't played since the Week 4 loss to Georgia and played fewer than 10 snaps in back-to-back weeks before suffering a calf strain. He'll battle with Jonathan Hatton for the third running back carries as Lloyd Avant and Tory Blaylock have established themselves as the Sooners' 1-2 punch in the running back rotation. Defensively, the Oklahoma Sooners have big questions. Rotation linebacker Cole Sullivan was ruled out for this week. Safety Peyton Bowen and cornerback Eli Bowen are both questionable for Week 9. Both Bowens are key pieces to the Sooners' defense, and against a good South Carolina passing attack, Peyton Bowen's presence is critical. He's one of the best safeties in college football. If he can't play, it'll be Omarion Robinson and Michael Boganowski starting at the safety spots, and potentially Reggie Powers mixing into the rotation. If Eli Bowen is out, Trystan Haynes would likely get another start. He's been solid since entering the starting lineup against the Texas Longhorns and would need to be at his best this week if called upon to start. Injuries have once again been a key storyline for the Sooners in the 2026 season. If the key players listed as questionable and probable can be available for this week, it would give the Sooners a boost on both sides of the football. home.blurb: South Carolina vs. Oklahoma injury report: Jawarn Howell, Quay'Sheed Scott ruled out Skip to main content About On Thursday evening, just two days before the Gamecocks are set to kick off, South Carolina head coach Shane Beamer announced that Gamecock running back Jawarn Howell and defensive back Quay'Sheed Scott will both be out for Saturday's game. Coach Beamer gave the update during his weekly radio show, stating that both guys will be out for the game against the Sooners. “It will say that ‘Sheed is out again this week,” Beamer said via Gamecock Central . “He’s got some tests that have to get done tomorrow, and we’re optimistic on what those test will say, and if they say what we hope it’s going to say, he’ll be playing next week against Texas A&M. Jawarn won’t play Saturday; he banged his shoulder up, I guess Wednesday, in practice last week or maybe it was Friday, but late in the week. He was available last week in the Tennessee game, just has still been bothering him, and we thought the best thing for him was just still to be able to rest that shoulder a little bit this week and get that healthy. So those two are out.” Scott has not played since South Carolina's Oct. 3 game at home against the Kentucky Wildcats. The Gamecocks starting nickelback left the game and did not return, even having to be hospitalized as a precaution. Coach Beamer has not disclosed the specifics regarding his injury. Howell has also missed time this season with an injury, as he did not play in last week's win over Tennessee. Although his status changed from doubtful to questionable throughout the week last week ahead of the game against the Vols, he was ruled out and did not play. South Carolina Football All-Time LIsts South Carolina Football Recruiting South Carolina Basketball All-Time Lists South Carolina Basketball Recruiting The South Carolina Gamecocks will be without two players as the team seeks a third-straight victory over Oklahoma on Saturday. The running back has been a nice complement to South Carolina's backfield, led by Jabree Coleman and Matt Fuller. Through four games, Howell has rushed for 104 yards on 18 carries, averaging 5.8 yards per rush. Scott has nine total tackles with three passes defended so far this season. South Carolina will have a tough task going on the road against Oklahoma. The Sooners have notched victories over Texas and Mississippi State this season, and have the same record as South Carolina at 4-3. The Gamecocks are listed as 3.5-point road underdogs . picks.headline: Staff Predictions: Florida State Seminoles vs. Clemson Tigers
picks.blurb: Staff Predictions: Florida State Seminoles vs. Clemson Tigers | Tomahawk Nation Skip to main content SB Nation SB Nation logo A Florida State Seminoles Community Tomahawk Nation October 31, 2026 Tomahawk Nation Notifications Notifications The Feed Betting Betting News FanDuel College Football Odds FanDuel College Basketball Odds Florida State Football Odds Florida State Basketball Odds College Football Picks and Predictions College Basketball Picks and Predictions Login / Sign Up Search The Feed Betting Expand Betting News Community Guidelines All communities Notifications Florida State Football FSU looks to get to .500 and avoid 3rd straight loss as home favorites The Florida State Seminoles will host the Clemson Tigers this Saturday for a Halloween evening rivalry game at Doak Campbell Stadium in Tallahassee. The kickoff is scheduled for 7:00 p.m., and the game will be televised by the ACCN. This will be the 39th meeting between the teams, with Florida State (3-4, 1-3 ACC) leading the all-time series 21-17, including a 12-7 record at Doak and an 18-15 record as ACC members. However, Clemson has won the last two meetings and holds a 15-7 advantage over the last 22 games, including wins in nine of the last 10 meetings. Clemson will be attempting to win a fifth consecutive game at Doak, becoming only the third program ever to win five consecutive road games against FSU in Tallahassee, joining Florida (six straight from 1966-76) and Miami (Fla.) (five from 1957-77). Despite Clemson (4-3, 2-2 ACC) and Florida State combining for 13 of the last 15 ACC championships, both teams are struggling this year. Clemson’s losses have come against #15 LSU, #1 Miami, and a 6-2 Virginia Tech team that scored the winning touchdown with 1:44 left on the clock. FSU’s four losses were in double overtime at #1 Miami, at #10 Alabama, at home against #19 SMU, and at Louisville when the defense totally collapsed. Clemson’s defense is the strength of their team. The Tigers rank 32nd in total defense (317), 36th in passing (186), T-53rd in rushing defense (131), T-30th in third-down defense (holding opponents to a 33.3-percent conversion rate), have allowed only four passing touchdowns, and have recorded 20 sacks through seven games. The Tigers’ passing offense, behind true freshman QB Tait Reynolds, who was named starter following an injury to Christopher Vizzina in their 2nd game, has only thrown one touchdown, and the 2 QBs combined have only thrown 2 TDs all season. Reynolds has been sacked 20 times this season and has thrown 3 interceptions while averaging just 6.1 yards per completion. Overall, Clemson has allowed 21 sacks, rank 115th in total offense (333). 112th in scoring offense, 115th in passing offense, 126th in 3rd-down conversion (31.7%), and 93rd in red zone offense. Florida State looks to avoid its 3rd straight loss after a heartbreaking double-overtime loss to Miami. The Noles were able to rush for 138 yards against the nation’s #1-ranked rushing defense; however, leading rusher Ousmane Kromah sustained a lower-leg injury and will miss the rest of the 2026 season. FSU loses double-overtime heartbreaker to Miami Social media reactions to the end of FSU vs. Miami Column: ACC replay review never entertained another outcome on FSU’s final play FSU running back Ousmane Kromah carted off near the end of first half against Miami Despite having a losing season record, FSU’s offense is ranked T-49th in the nation in total offense, 50th in scoring, 46th in rushing, 63rd in passing, and 34th in red-zone offense. FSU individual leaders After allowing Miami to rack up 583 total yards on 78 plays for a 7.5 yard average/play, FSU’s defense now ranks 130th in the nation, giving up 435 yards/game, 124th in passing defense (256 yards/game), T-112th in third-down percentage, allowing opponents to convert nearly 43% of the time on third-down attempts, and T-104th in first-down defense, allowing their opponents 155 first downs (22.1/game) in the 7 games played this season. Florida State is currently trending as a 5.5-point favorite with the over/under set at 49.5 points, according to FanDuel. 2026 FSU Schedule Preview: Clemson Tigers Read what your TOMAHAWK NATION PROGNOSTICATORS think about this Saturday’s showdown. Then look over and digest all the FREE PRE-GAME CONTENT we’ve posted leading up to this game. We would love to hear your thoughts about how you feel about this game and your final score prediction in the comments. Jordan Silversmith (season record: 6-1) This game is a tricky one to call. I do not think Clemson is a good football team. However, they probably have the best unit on the field: their defense. Another issue for Florida State is that the Seminoles have historically struggled against the Tigers, with no home wins in the last decade. Even so, FSU should win on Saturday night. I imagine that, off a bye, head coach Mike Norvell will scheme up points on the opening drive, and Tony White’s defense should make forcing CU to throw the name of the game. This game will be close, as it often is with FSU, but Clemson isn’t good enough right now to win a rivalry game on the road. Seminole win, but no cover. FSU 27, Clemson 24 Tim Scribble (season record: 6-1) This could be a scary game, fitting for Halloween. With Kromah out, Clemson’s defense may keep FSU in check but the Tiger’s offense is dreadful. If Clemson somehow overwhelm’s Tony White’s defense, that relationship needs to end. I think FSU wins but it will be ugly. FSU 24, Clemson 17 Jacob Smith (season record: 3-2 ) Call me crazy, but this game is going to be completely unwatchable but FSU will emerge victorious. Firstly, it’s at Doak. On Halloween. Where else would you rather be? In all seriousness, Clemson’s offensive efficiency is dreadful. Like, REALLY dreadful. Per Game On Paper , Clemson’s EPA per pass is #136 out of #138 and their EPA per rush is #110. They are only 33.7% successful on third down, good for #128, and they are just bad at most things offense, mainly because their QB is a freshman. Their defense is good to great, though! #13 in EPA/Pass defense and just middle of the pack on rushing defense, #64 in the nation. Florida State meanwhile… their defense is trash. #127 on EPA per pass, #105 on EPA per rush, #120 on 3rd/4th down stops. The offense is good, though. #39 in EPA/Pass, #36 in EPA/Rush. If they can handle Clemson’s terrible offense and do good things on defense against a very not good Clemson offense, it might be a fun halloweekend in Tallahassee. Give me the Noles to pull off, not an upset per se, just a good, scrappy win. Florida State 14, Clemson 13 Curt Weiler (season record: 5-2, 2-5 ATS) Call me crazy for buying in again but I think I believe in this FSU team more than I do that Clemson team. The Tigers’ defense is pretty good. But the offense is very bad. Clemson is the only FBS team which has scored more points from its defense/special teams than its offense . To Tony White and his unit, I would say “If not now, when?” FSU 27, Clemson 20 NoleThruandThru (season record: 7-0) I’m taking a break from the Marshawn gag this week to honor my dad, who passed away two weeks ago. The world lost a wonderful FSU alum and fan, and I hope he enjoys this one from heaven. FSU 28, Clemson 24 Jon Marchant (season record: 6-1 ) Nobody knows what kind of team FSU will be from week to week. No result is off the table and there’s no score that would surprise anyone. So I’m picking FSU this week. Just cause. Also, it’s funny when Dabo loses. Clemson 23, FSU 28 LastNoleOfKrypton (season record: 5-1) I’m picking FSU but I don’t feel great about the prediction. I’m really worried about what FSU’s offense will look like without Kromah vs. Clemson’s defense. That being said I have not seen enough from Clemson’s offense to stay off the field and if you give FSU’s skill group enough shots they’re going to get points. Noles win. FSU 24 Clemson 17 Matt Minnick (Season record: 5-2; ATS: 4-3) As others have said, Clemson’s offense is putrid. Two passing touchdowns all season long is nearly unfathomable. But is Tony White’s defense just what the doctor ordered? It’s the moveable object vs the stoppable force. I’ve said all year that despite all the suckage over the last three seasons, FSU has honestly been pretty decent at home. However, Norvell’s teams also have a penchant for finding ways to lose very winnable games. If Kromah was healthy, I’d feel a lot better about the ‘Noles. If Quindarious Jones was healthy I’d feel a lot better about the ‘Noles. If a random FCS DC who’s name was drawn out of a hat was FSU’s defensive coordinator, I’d feel a lot better about the ‘Noles. Clemson 30 , FSU 28 Frank DNole (season record: 3-4) FSU’s offense is better than Clemson’s defense. Clemson’s offense is about as good as FSU’s defense. Advantage Noles. This will be the game that turns the program around, and everything comes together for the Noles. The Noles are 5.5-point favorites for a reason. Vegas knows something and the Seminoles know it too. The game will follow a similar storyline to what we witnessed against Virginia. The Seminoles will win the offensive, defensive, and special teams battles because the FSU players will give 110% more effort, they will want it more, and they will play with more heart than their equally talented Clempsun opponent. FSU Seminoles 34, Orange Dabo’s 27 P erry Kostidakis (season record: 4-3, 3-4 ATS) For all its flaws over the last two seasons, FSU has taken care of business against the teams it should beat while in the confines of Doak. I have faith in FSU’s ability to get enough points against a stout Clemson defense and, as naive as it might be, take care of business against a dreadful Tigers offense. picks.blurb: Clemson Tigers final odds and prediction for Week 9 at Florida State Seminoles Skip to main content Recruiting Women's sports Men's basketball Women's basketball Baseball and softball FanSided NCAA Sites Clemson has been left with no choice but to pick up the pieces after last week's soul-crushing loss to Virginia Tech. It may have only counted as one defeat on the ledger, but it really did feel like 2.5 losses mentally. For better or worse, the Tigers must turn the page and get ready for potentially a wild road game at the rival Florida State Seminoles. It will be during Halloween, nevertheless, so get ready for it. Clemson enters play at 4-3 on the season and 2-2 in the ACC. It has wins over Georgia Southern, North Carolina, Cal, and Charleston Southern, with losses to LSU, Miami, and Virginia Tech. While Florida State is only 3-4 on the season, Mike Norvell's Seminoles have a knack for scoring points and playing some fairly competitive football at home. Dabo Swinney cannot let his team overlook FSU. With that all in mind, here are the latest betting odds, how to watch this game, and a game prediction. Latest betting odds for Clemson Tigers at Florida State Seminoles According to the FanDuel Sportsbook , Florida State will be laying 5.5 points to visiting Clemson. The associated moneylines for this game are Florida State -215 and Clemson +180. This means that it would take a $215 bet on Florida State to win $100, while wagering $100 on Clemson would pocket you $180. The projected point total for the game comes in at a combined 49.5 points, down from 51.5. Using all of that information above, a projected final score for this game would be something in the vicinity of Florida State 27.5, Clemson 22. While the odds for this game have fluctuated a bit , Florida State has been the favorite throughout for two reasons. It is a home game for the Seminoles, and the meager Tigers' offense has struggled to score points against Power Four competition all season long. Game odds refresh periodically and are subject to change. If you or someone you know has a gambling problem and wants help, call 1-800-GAMBLER. How to watch Clemson Tigers at Florida State Seminoles Here is what you need to know to be able to watch Clemson take on Florida State on Halloween night. Date: Saturday, Oct. 31 Time: 7:00 p.m. ET Location: Tallahassee, FL Venue: Doak Campbell Stadium TV Info: ACCN Streaming Info: fuboTV Radio: 105.5 FM (The Roar)/Clemson Athletic Network Kickoff from Doak Campbell Stadium in Tallahassee, FL, will be at 7:00 p.m. ET on Saturday, Oct. 31. The ACC Network will carry the conference rivalry game. You can stream the game on fuboTV. You can listen to the game over the airwaves on 105.5 FM The Roar, or you can check out any other radio affiliates on the Clemson Athletic Network. You are not going to want to miss this rivalry game! Clemson Tigers at Florida State Seminoles game prediction This high-stakes ACC rivalry game will come down to one of two things. From the Florida State perspective, it will be all about how disciplined the Seminoles' pass defense will be. This team can score points, but it does love to give them up in bunches. As for Clemson, the Tigers need to show on offense that they can put up 30 or so points if they need to get into some sort of a low-end shootout. Right now, it is so hard to fathom Clemson getting into the end zone at least three times on Saturday. The Tigers are going to need three touchdowns, and presumably 12 points from Nolan Hauser on special teams, to realistically have a chance at pulling off the upset. Gideon Davidson may get one on the ground, possibly two if he gets lucky. This will come down to whether Tait Reynolds can throw for one. Unfortunately, Clemson's offense is not built right now to score quickly and in bunches, so it will lose. Week 9 final score prediction: Florida State 30, Clemson 24. picks.blurb: Clemson (4-3, 3-2 ACC) is coming off a last-minute 20-16 loss to the Virginia Tech Hokies at Memorial Stadium. The Tigers led for much of the second half, but Hokies quarterback Ethan Grunkemeyer led his team on an 11-play, 69-yard drive for the game-winning score with 1:44 to play. Grunkmeyer's 5-yard touchdown pass to tight end Luke Reynolds on fourth-and-1 gave Virginia Tech its first win over Clemson in 19 years and dropped the Tigers to 2-8 in their last 10 home games against Power Four opponents. The offense struggled once again, netting only 288 total yards and going 3 of 14 on third downs. Freshman QB Tait Reynolds completed 20 of his 26 passes, but his average completion went for only 5.9 yards. The Tigers rank dead last in the ACC and just 115th nationally in total offense with 333.1 yards per game. Clemson will face a Florida State (3-4, 1-3) team fresh off a bye, and one that should be playing with plenty of confidence. Mike Norvell's Seminoles took the top-ranked Miami Hurricanes into double overtime before falling 43-35 at Hard Rock Stadium on Oct. 17. Fifth-year senior Ashton Daniels leads the Seminoles' passing attack and has 1,618 yards and 12 touchdowns to eight interceptions in seven games this season. Daniels threw four touchdown passes and rushed for another score in FSU's loss to Miami in Week 7. Clemson has won nine of the last 10 meetings against Florida State dating back to 2015. Will the Tigers' run of dominance in the rivalry continue or end Saturday in Tallahassee? Will Clemson football beat Florida State? ESPN's prediction Oddsmakers have Florida State as a 6.5-point favorite over Clemson, but as always, ESPN Analytics has its own odds for Saturday's game. ESPN's matchup predictor , which offers a prediction model based on its college football power index and other variables, doesn't favor the Tigers, either. It gives Florida State a 71.9% chance to win and Clemson a 28.1% chance. The Tigers are 51st nationally in ESPN's FPI with a 5.8 rating, which ranks 11th among the 17 ACC teams. Florida State has a 10.1 FPI rating that's 37th nationally. The Tigers are one spot ahead of Kansas State (5.7) and one spot below Virginia (6.0). picks.blurb: Clemson (4-3, 2-2 ACC) and Florida State (3-4, 1-3), which have played every year since 1992 with the exception of 2020, are both at a crossroads. Neither program wants to move on from its coach and pay a hefty buyout, but neither team has shown very much on the field lately to offer hope. The Tigers suffered a 20-16 gut-punch loss to Virginia Tech in Week 8. It marked Clemson's eighth in its last 10 games against a Power Four opponent at home. The Tigers led for much of the second half until Ethan Grunkemeyer's game-winning 5-yard touchdown pass on fourth-and-1 with 1:44 left. Florida State came within a play or two of adding to the chaos that was college football's thrilling Week 7 slate. The Seminoles took Miami to double overtime before falling 43-35 at Hard Rock Stadium. FSU quarterback Ashton Daniels accounted for five touchdowns in the loss, including four through the air. Clemson hasn't thrown four touchdowns all season. Tait Reynolds, the 19-year-old true freshman who was thrust into the starting job following an injury to Christopher Vizzina, is averaging just 6.1 yards per completion and has been sacked 20 times in seven games behind a weak offensive line. Clemson ranks 115th nationally in total offense with 333.1 yards per game, which is last in the ACC. Florida State ranks 49th with 414.3 total yards per games. Here's ESPN's prediction for Saturday's game. Will Clemson football beat Florida State? ESPN's final score prediction Ahead of Clemson-Florida State, ESPN's Bill Connelly predicted the final score using his popular SP+ metrics . Connelly has the Seminoles winning their first game against the Tigers at Doak Campbell Stadium since 2014. The oddsmakers' latest 5.5 spread favors FSU, as well. Connelly's final score prediction: Florida State 27, Clemson 24. He gives the Seminoles a win probability of 59%. Where Clemson, Florida State sit in ESPN SP+ rankings entering Week 9 rivalry Clemson is No. 55 in ESPN's SP+ team rankings , up one spot from last week despite the loss to Virginia Tech. The Tigers have an overall rating of 4.7, up from 4.0 a week ago. Clemson is one spot ahead of UCF in ESPN's overall team rankings. To break down Clemson's rating by unit, SP+ gives the Tigers a 23.3 rating on offense (No. 97 nationally, up one spot from last week) and a 19.0 rating on defense, which is 25th nationally and is the same as before the Tigers' loss to the Hokies. In special teams, Clemson has a 0.5 rating, which ranks 10th-best in the nation. Florida State is No. 54 in the SP+ team rankings with an overall rating of 5.8, one spot below Virginia and one ahead of Clemson. The metrics give the Seminoles a 32.7 rating on offense that's No. 32 nationally, a 27.1 rating on defense that's No. 76, and a 0.2 rating in special teams that's 43rd in the country. What are ESPN SP+ rankings? According to Connelly, SP+ is "simply a measure of the most sustainable and predictable aspects of football. If you're lucky or unimpressive in a win, your rating will probably fall. If you're strong and unlucky in a loss, it will probably rise." "SP+ is not a résumé ranking, so it does not automatically give credit for big wins or particularly brave scheduling -- no good predictive system does," he adds. picks.blurb: Clemson Predicted to Drop Another Game vs Florida State This Week ClemsonRoundtable 144 Members • 1,127 Posts ClemsonRoundtable ClemsonRoundtable Related stories Trending stories Ken Ruinard / USA Today Network South Ca Ken Ruinard / USA Today Network South Ca Clemson Predicted to Drop Another Game vs Florida State This Week Matt Levine Partner Oct 29, 2026 7:43 PM Published Oct 29, 2026 7:43 PM The Clemson Tigers could be in some trouble this weekend. The Clemson Tigers will be heading out on the road for a big game against the Florida State Seminoles this week. Clemson comes into the contest with a record of 4-3 on the season, having lost last week to Virginia Tech. Florida State will be entering the game with a record of 3-4 for the season, looking to defend home field this week. In a new prediction from college football analyst David Kenyon of Bleacher Report , Clemson will struggle in this game against Florida State. Kenyon has the Tigers dropping the game to the Seminoles by a score of 24-19. If this prediction were to come true, it would send the Tigers into some real trouble, with them falling to 4-4 on the season. There have already been calls for head coach Dabo Swinney to be let go of before the year started, and if the team can't turn things around, it will only grow louder. Related stories For Clemson to avoid dropping the game to Florida State, the offense is going to have to get going. The Tigers have been carried by their defense all season long, with the offensive attack falling way behind. Quarterback Tait Reynolds has struggled in his first action in college, and he has limited what this Tigers team can do. For the year, Reynolds has thrown for just 1,096 yards with one touchdown and three interceptions. Reynolds has seen problems trying to push the ball down the field, and the offense has been ineffective due to this. Clemson has to find some sort of footing offensively if they want to take down Florida State on the road this week. Due to the struggles of Reynolds, there have been calls for the Tigers to make a switch at the quarterback position. But for now, Swinney seems content to go with Reynolds, even though he had previously said that a change could be made. Christopher Vizzina entered the year as the starter, but was then benched after just two weeks for Reynolds. Vizzina did suffer an injury, but he has remained on the bench due to performance, according to Swinney. If the Tigers were to drop this game to the Seminoles, the calls for Vizzina to return would likely continue. Swinney would then have some choices to make, especially with the season starting to spiral out of control for the team. Kickoff for the game between the Tigers and Seminoles is scheduled for 4:00 p.m. PT/7:00 p.m. ET from Doak S. Campbell Stadium.

away.blurb: Crutchfield has been in and out of FSU's lineup this season as he battles injuries, but the coaching staff has been extremely pleased with what he can do, and Norvell is "hopeful" he will be available this week. "I think Jordan Crutchfield is trending well to be able to get back in the secondary," Norvell said. "We've had some guys that have been banged up there as well. Jordan's a guy that has shown some flashes here, just dealt with some minor injuries that have kind of set him back just from the consistency of his opportunities, but expecting him to get some good work here this week and hopefully be available." The update was less positive about Nichelson, who hasn't played since the game against the New Mexico State Aggies, and Norvell doesn't expect that to change this week. He is "hopeful" that the rest of the linebackers will be able to play after several were in and out of the Miami game with injuries. home.headline: Florida State injury updates: Mike Norvell expects key returns, but timing is an issue
home.blurb: Florida State coach Mike Norvell recently provided a couple of injury updates on multiple Seminoles who have missed significant time this season. Injuries have been a huge issue for the team this year for Norvell, particularly on defense, where multiple players are out for the season. Sometimes injuries can make or break a team, and so far, the Seminoles have been able to do quite a bit with multiple contributors sidelined. Norvell kicked off his injury updates portion of the press conference with a quick tidbit on linebacker Blake Nichelson, who has not played since the season opener against New Mexico State. Nichelson is nearing a return, and while the game against Clemson might still be out of reach , the linebacker should be able to return to play soon. Samuel Singleton Jr.'s return would be huge for the Florida State offense Norvell is not giving up on Singleton's return; he never ruled the running back out for the season, and he clearly still thinks there is hope for his return. It might be a delusion at this point from Norvell to avoid the reality that Florida State is in a bad spot at running back, or a future return this season might still truly be in the cards. I personally would like to think that Singleton is close to coming back, and the faster he can return, the better for Florida State. Tre Wisner is an experienced running back, but he has not been the most effective player in a short sample size this season. Aside from Wisner, there is not much of an experienced supporting cast. Additionally, Florida State might be in trouble if Singleton is not able to return this season due to the fact that there are only three healthy running backs. The Seminoles truly cannot afford to have another running back go down with an injury, and if Singleton is not available for another two or three weeks, that could be an issue. The timing of Crutchfield's return could not be any better, with Quindarrius Jones, Nehemiah Chandler, and Ashlynd Barker all dealing with injuries. Barker has been playing through his injury thanks to a cast, but Crutchfield can do it all in the secondary, and he should be able to take some pressure off multiple players. The Seminoles might have help on the way at linebacker, but there are still concerns Getting an experienced player like Nichelson back would be huge for the Seminoles, but the reality is that the linebacker room is still very banged up.
