home.headline: Quindarrius Jones injury update: Florida State's banged-up secondary continues to take hits
home.blurb: With the game against Clemson quickly approaching for Florida State, a top defensive back has been ruled out. Starting corner Quindarrius Jones left the game against Miami in Week 7 after playing just 14 snaps. Jones had a week to recover with the bye, which brought some hope, but the defender will not be able to play against Clemson. Jones has missed two games this season now after sitting out the home game against Central Arkansas earlier in the year. Frankly, it was better for the defense to play Central Arkansas without him, so more defensive backs would be able to see the field. However, against Clemson, Florida State cannot afford to suffer another injury at an already weak position. The secondary has been torn to shreds all year, with Karson Hobbs and Jamari Howard spending the majority of the season on the injury report. Jones has missed time, freshman Jordan Crutchfield has been unavailable most of the season, and Chuck Kennon was dismissed just as he began to recover from an injury. With Jones out, two players will likely take over: Charles Lester III and Jordan Crutchfield, who will be making his return from an injury against Clemson. Lester has been the main replacement for Jones this season, playing 33 snaps against Miami after Jones left the game. Lester also replaced Jones for the game against Central Arkansas, logging 34 snaps. Jones typically plays between 45 and 55 snaps each week, with his total number of snaps played increasing as the injuries in the secondary have stacked up. Lester has been covering a good portion of the missing snaps, but against Miami, Ja'Bril Rawls played 74 out of 80 possible snaps, which is something he has done multiple times this season. Lester is more than likely going to resume the same role he has previously taken when Jones is forced to sit out, but the addition of a healthy Crutchfield gives the staff options. Fellow safety KJ Kirkland is expected to play, but has been dealing with an injury, which could create a different avenue to the field for Crutchfield. In limited playing time this season, Lester has proven to be effective at times, with eight total tackles, including three against Miami after Jones left the game. Lester has struggled at times in coverage, but his ability to recover and limit additional gains is notable. Starters have to play virtually the entire game to compensate for the fact that there is no depth, and the result has been a tired defense that often falls apart late in games. Jones missing the game against Clemson certainly hurts, but the Seminoles have been in this position multiple times already this season, and a plan is likely already in place. away.headline: Malachi Toney injury update: Star Miami receiver briefly leaves game vs Pitt
away.blurb: Star wide receiver Malachi Toney , one of the leading contenders for the Heisman Trophy, asked to be taken out of the game and jogged gingerly off the field after a five-yard catch in the second quarter. On a 1st-and-19 following a personal foul penalty that wiped out a 36-yard run from Mark Fletcher, Toney caught a short pass from Darian Mensah for a five-yard pickup. As he was trying to evade Pitt defenders, though, Toney appeared to tweak something. After being taken down to the turf at Hard Rock Stadium, he came up and motioned to the sideline to be taken out of the game before jogging gingerly off the field. Once on the sideline, Toney went into the injury tent. After coming out, he remained with a helmet on and was limping while doing exercises on the sideline, according to the ESPN broadcast. He wasn't out long. After Pitt scored a touchdown to trim its deficit to 10, 17-7, Toney was back in the game for the Hurricanes to start their next drive. He made his presence felt, too, hauling in a 21-yard reception on third-and-18 from the Miami 31-yard line before later breaking off a 53-yard touchdown reception to pad his team's lead back to 17. Still, the Hurricanes encountered an unexpected and unwelcome obstacle. More: College football Week 8 schedule looks quiet. Here's where chaos could strike It interrupted a stellar day for the sophomore, who had already hauled in nine catches for 73 yards and a touchdown. Where do things stand for Toney? Here's the latest on his injury: After the touchdown grab, Toney had 11 catches for 147 yards and two touchdowns. It's the fifth time in seven games this season that he's amassed at least 110 receiving yards in a game and he's three yards shy of his third game with at least 150 receiving yards. Heading into Saturday's game against Pitt, the Miami-area native had 50 catches for 758 yards and eight touchdowns. He's fourth among all FBS players in receiving yards per game and is tied for fifth in touchdown receptions. North Carolina fans are ready for the college basketball season, but a couple of things need to be considered before Monday night as it takes on Western Carolina. North Carolina should be able to win this game no matter who's on the court for them, but it's also important to note that some injuries are currently being factored in. The biggest is Matt Able, the North Carolina State transfer expected to be one of the better players on the roster this season. Able missed the exhibition game against Charlotte, though it hasn't been reported yet what happened. According to Rodd Baxley, who was at the game, the injury didn't look noticeable. State transfer, is one of 11 newcomers on coach Michael Malone's first roster in Chapel Hill. The all-white Stormtroopers have served as the primary road look, and at home they have worn the traditional white helmet, orange jersey and white pants combination against Florida A&M and Florida State. The Buckeyes (6-1, 4-0 Big Ten) will try to maintain their No. 2 ranking Saturday night and attempt to knock off a desperate USC Trojans (6-2, 3-2 Big Ten) team still fighting for their CFP lives. With kickoff drawing closer, how does a Buckeyes team no longer led by quarterback Julian Sayin fare on the road? Scroll to find this week’s staff predictions, as I am all alone in first place at 7-0 so far this season. Bickel/Dispatch] | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect Date: Saturday, Oct. 31 Date: Saturday, Oct. 31 Time: 7:30 p.m. ET/4:30 p.m. PT TV Channel: NBC (consult TV Guide or preferred streaming provider for details). Odds : Ohio State -6.5 ; over/under is 51.5 (via DraftKings Sportsbook) Location : Los Angeles Memorial Coliseum – Los Angeles, Calif. Ohio State’s record under Ryan Day : 88-13 (8-6 in postseason bowl games/CFP). Last time vs. USC: 2017 Cotton Bowl: Ohio State won 24-7, when the Trojans were still members of the Pac-12. USC leads the all-time series 13-10-1 since 1937. Ohio State so far this season: 6-1 (4-0 Big Ten) Zain Bando : 7-0 Dylan Buganski : 6-1 Rafael Zamorano : 4-1 (no pick in Week 6 or Week 7) Chip Minnich : 5-0 (began contributing ahead of Week 3) Zain Bando: Ohio State 21, USC 17 After a week off, Ohio State continues its quest for a Big Ten and national title. It’ll just be without Julian Sayin as its starting quarterback. Since Sayin went down, Ohio State on SI (and I included) have done our best to bring Buckeye Nation as many perspectives as possible as the season resumes Saturday night in Los Angeles against the USC Trojans. Given the parity in this year's wacky college football season, the Buckeyes have yet to have a true reality-check moment. This week isn’t it either. The Badgers, who play the Iowa Hawkeyes earlier in the day’s action, suffocated the Trojans in all areas last week in Madison in one of the sport’s most shocking upsets. Although Halloween night could call for a spooky outcome (pun purposely intended), it’s hard to pick against Ohio State in Big Ten play, regardless of who the quarterback ends up being, until it loses in league play. So far, I’m the lone undefeated picker this season, so riding the hot hand with coach Ryan Day’s team against a depleted Trojans bunch seems like a smart pick (although all-time series history says otherwise). Rafael Zamorano: Ohio State 24, USC 14 Ohio State has reached the crux of its season, not necessarily because of where they stand in Big Ten competition at this point in its schedule, but because we don’t know for sure what the Buckeyes will look like without star quarterback Julian Sayin for the foreseeable future. Not to take anything away from the 6-2 Trojans, but what was originally supposed to be a road game against a solid-but-not-elite conference opponent has now shifted its focus entirely on how the Buckeyes will look with a freshman starting at quarterback, be it true freshman Luke Fahey or redshirt freshman Tavien St. Clair. Having said that, Ohio State still wields a deeper and more talented roster overall, headlined by the best player in the game, wide receiver Jeremiah Smith. The Buckeyes’ staff has more than enough resources to work with to keep whichever quarterback ends up starting well protected scheme-wise. Look for a lot of quick passes and screens on offense, while the defense figures out a way to pressure Jayden Maiava into committing mistakes, just like Wisconsin did last week. With the Buckeyes being favored by a touchdown on the spread (-7), I’m picking them to cover thanks to another solid performance on defense. Chip Minnich: Ohio State 24, USC 21 The Wisconsin Badgers’ 24-7 win over USC last Saturday has Ohio State fans understandably wondering whether the Buckeyes will follow a comparable game plan. I am guessing that Luke Fahey will be the starting quarterback, and that the coaching staff has emphasized to Fahey to play efficiently in a style reminiscent of when Julian Sayin made his first start at home vs. Texas in 2025. The USC defensive line has the pass rushing ability to get after an opposing quarterback, and I believe Fahey will use his legs to get out of the pocket and make positive yards to keep drives alive. Ohio State's defense is going to be tested all game against a formidable USC offense, despite the issues that the Trojans had last week in Madison. Maybe it's wishful thinking on my part, but this game has some serious Tresselball vibes for me going into Saturday night against an USC team that has its back to the wall. Yards and points may be difficult for the Buckeyes to earn, but I believe the Buckeyes will exhale when Connor Hawkins makes a late field goal in the final minutes of the contest. Dylan Buganski: Ohio State 24, USC 14 For the first time during Ryan Day’s tenure as Ohio State head coach, a backup quarterback will start for the Buckeyes in a Big Ten matchup. It is still unknown if that starter will be true freshman Luke Fahey, or former 5-star sophomore Tavien St. Clair. Although, what is known coming into this matchup is that the USC defense has been one of the worst defenses against the pass in the Big Ten this season. Learning curves should be there for whatever quarterback is penciled to start in Los Angeles against the Trojans, but Heisman favorite Jeremiah Smith and the other pass-catchers in this room should still perform well and keep the Buckeye offense afloat. The run game will also be watched closely, as more will be expected from this group and it'll get a good test against a strong USC front. USC quarterback Jayden Maiava should make some plays to keep this game competitive, but expect the Ohio State front to stifle an inconsistent rushing attack from the Trojans and force some turnovers to swing the momentum in the Buckeyes’ favor, giving them their 6th straight win and first at USC since 1946. picks.blurb: Rece Davis Jumps Off USC Bandwagon With Ohio State Prediction Before Halloween Clash Skip to main content SI.COM TRANSFER PORTAL More from CFB-HQ On SI NEWS ESPN College GameDay host Rece Davis is siding with No. 2 Ohio State in its Halloween night trip to USC, even with a true freshman quarterback likely making his first career start against coach Lincoln Riley’s Trojans. Davis made his pick on the College GameDay Podcast, betting star receiver Jeremiah Smith helps Ohio State end a regular-season drought at the Coliseum that dates to 1946. “I’ll take the Buckeyes,” Davis said after USC’s 24-7 loss at Wisconsin pushed him off the Trojans’ bandwagon. Rece Davis picks Ohio State at USC USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect Davis isn’t sold on the 6-1 Buckeyes yet. “Ohio State comes in ranked second in the nation and, at least to my way of thinking, a bit of a placeholder until I see what they’ve got at quarterback,” he said. Davis isn’t sold on the 6-1 Buckeyes yet. “Ohio State comes in ranked second in the nation and, at least to my way of thinking, a bit of a placeholder until I see what they’ve got at quarterback,” he said. He does like the setup for true freshman Luke Fahey, whose paternal grandparents met as students at Ohio State . “Fahey is a Southern California kid. I believe his grandparents actually met at Ohio State. So there’s a connection,” Davis said. “He gets to make his first start in his backyard, figuratively, from where he grew up. I think he’ll be fine.” The Buckeyes haven’t won a regular-season game at USC since a 21-0 shutout in 1946 and haven’t scored a touchdown at the Coliseum since 1949, losing their last four visits there by a combined 126-9 . Davis is counting on Ohio State’s Heisman Trophy contender at receiver to fix that. “I’ll bet you that changes with Jeremiah Smith,” he said. Who replaces Julian Sayin at quarterback? USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect Julian Sayin, Ohio State’s starting quarterback, hurt his throwing arm in a 19-15 win over Indiana on Oct. 17 and is expected to miss at least the rest of the regular season. Head coach Ryan Day hasn’t named a starter, with Fahey and former five-star recruit Tavien St. Clair both taking first-team reps during the bye week. Julian Sayin, Ohio State’s starting quarterback, hurt his throwing arm in a 19-15 win over Indiana on Oct. 17 and is expected to miss at least the rest of the regular season. Head coach Ryan Day hasn’t named a starter, with Fahey and former five-star recruit Tavien St. Clair both taking first-team reps during the bye week. “I’m not going to,” Day said Wednesday when asked if he’d name a starting quarterback . “But both guys had a good week of practice and I think both will be ready to play.” Day also said it’s “definitely possible” both quarterbacks play. Fahey replaced Sayin against Indiana, but Ohio State played conservatively with a late lead and both of his pass attempts fell incomplete. I’m off the bandwagon,” he said. USC (6-2, 3-2 Big Ten) fell out of the AP Top 25 after finishing with minus-17 rushing yards against the Badgers. Riley, who is 41-20 at USC and carries a reported $70 million buyout , addressed his future Tuesday. “This is where I want to be. This is the right place for me. I’m the right person to be here ,” he said. Davis expects a lopsided result to add to that conversation, though he cautioned USC against a quick change. “Ohio State goes in there and rolls and creates even more discussion around the future of USC,” Davis said. “Although, be very careful. You don’t know that you’re going to get someone that’s better. It’s not like Lincoln Riley’s a bad coach. It just hasn’t been quite to the level that they’ve expected up to this point.” Kickoff at the Los Angeles Memorial Coliseum is set for 7:30 p.m. ET Saturday on NBC. Photo By - Reuters Connect. Jaylen McClain (8) leads Ohio State against USC and Jayden Maiava (14) on Saturday night. In Ohio State's first game since losing Julian Sayin, the Buckeyes head across the country to take on a struggling USC program at Los Angeles Memorial Coliseum on Saturday, Oct. 31, at 7:30 p.m. ET (NBC). The Buckeyes are 6.5-point road favorites, and my Ohio State vs. USC predictions and college football picks are backing Matt Patricia's defense to hand Lincoln Riley another high-profile loss. TOP PICK Who will win Ohio State vs USC: Ohio State -6.5 Although Ryan Day hasn't made it official, it appears that true freshman Luke Fahey will be making his first start for Ohio State against USC. Even with the precarious QB situation, I would take the Buckeyes to cover up to -8.5 on the road against the Trojans. USC might be at an all-time low in the Lincoln Riley era after scoring just seven points and totaling 239 yards in a 17-point loss to Wisconsin last week, a game the Trojans were favored in. If USC's offense can't compete against top defenses, and Ohio State's is arguably the best (ranked No. 1 by SP+ ), Riley's team doesn't stand a chance. USC's defense has been atrocious under Gary Patterson, ranking 96th in success rate (46%) . Fahey and Jeremiah Smith , the Heisman Trophy odds favorite, should make enough plays to win a low-scoring game by nine or more points. Ohio State vs USC Over/Under pick: Under 51.5 USC's whole deal under Riley has been about having a strong enough offense to make up for poor defensive play. That hasn't been the case against quality programs, and this is USC's first taste of playing the Buckeyes since Riley took over. With Ohio State allowing just 13.4 points per game and holding six of seven opponents to fewer than 20 points, I like the Under at 49.5 or better . The Buckeyes' defense ranks fifth nationally in success rate (36.4%) , and USC is coming off an ugly outing against a Wisconsin defense that's a tier below the Buckeyes. But this is among the highest-ranked games in my Top 25 predictions this week because of Ohio State's QB situation. Fahey is a true freshman who was ranked the 38th-best QB in the 2026 recruiting class. The Buckeyes could struggle to score more than 27, even on this USC defense. Ohio State vs USC combo This is one of the best possible opponents for Fahey to make his debut against because of how awful USC's defense has been this season. The Trojans haven't even faced an offense ranked Top 25 by SP+ yet, and they're allowing 25 points per game . If Ohio State can score 25 on USC on a rainy night in L.A., the Buckeyes should cruise to a decisive win thanks to their defense. The Trojans have no run game and are asking too much of freshmen to carry the passing attack. Even if this game is tight heading into the fourth quarter, the Buckeyes will pull away. USC has been outscored 21-7 in the fourth quarter in its two losses this season. Ohio State vs. USC prediction: Why Buckeyes are in danger at Trojans
picks.blurb: Ohio State vs. USC prediction: Why Buckeyes are in danger at Trojans - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football College Football Playoff NFL injury tracker Belichick-Hudson breakup Brewers' championship parade Chet Holmgren injury Fantasy Start 'Em, Sit 'Em Ohio State vs. USC prediction: Why Buckeyes are in danger at Trojans Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Ohio State has been tabbed as a national championship favorite since this summer, but a major change at quarterback could make things interesting against USC this week. One of the more intriguing matchups on the Week 9 college football calendar finds the Buckeyes going on the road against the Trojans without Julian Sayin under center. How does that affect what happens in this battle of college football blue bloods? How Ohio State can win Ohio State Buckeyes wide receiver Jeremiah Smith (4) celebrates a touchdown with with wide receiver Devin McCuin (3) during the NCAA football game against the Indiana Hoosiers at Memorial Stadium Stadium in Bloomington, Ind. on Oct. 17, 2026. Credit: USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect (Reuters) Regardless of concerns at quarterback, Ohio State has the more complete statistical profile, particularly on defense. The Buckeyes are allowing just 13.4 points and 264.3 total yards per game, ranking fourth and sixth nationally, respectively. Their run defense has been especially effective, giving up only 92.9 rushing yards per game. It should have a decisive edge against a USC ground game that is 105th in FBS and totaling just 131 yards on average. Offensively, Jeremiah Smith has been spectacular yet again. The undefendable wide receiver and Heisman favorite has 984 receiving yards and 12 touchdowns on 52 catches. Even without Sayin, Ohio State can lean on its defense, establish Bo Jackson in the trenches, slow the game down, get the football into Smith's hands, and let him create after the catch. MORE: ESPN computer model offers bold prediction for Ohio State-USC game How USC can win Sep 4, 2026; Los Angeles, California, USA; Southern California Trojans quarterback Jayden Maiava (14) celebrates after a touchdown against the Fresno State Bulldogs in the first half at United Airlines Field at Los Angeles Memorial Coliseum. Mandatory Credit: Kirby Lee-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect (Reuters) Maybe relying on USC's defense to win a game hasn't always been a great idea. But they're in a very good position to exploit the Buckeyes' uncertainty at quarterback. Applying enough pressure on the edges to rattle Sayin's replacement could give this talented offense enough breathing room to make this interesting. The Trojans are averaging 303.6 passing yards per game, ranking 10th nationally, with quarterback Jayden Maiava throwing for 2,303 yards and 19 touchdowns. USC also converts 50.5 percent of its third downs, the 14th-best rate in the country. That ability to sustain drives could be important against an Ohio State defense that has allowed opponents to convert just 38 percent of third downs. The Trojans need Maiava to protect the football and attack downfield over top OSU's front line defenders. Defensively, USC must pressure the inexperienced Buckeyes quarterback and prevent him from developing any early rhythm. More: Predicting Big Ten football scores for Week 9's biggest games Who wins, and why? Make no mistake: the absence of Julian Sayin distributing to the Buckeyes' talented wideouts is a real problem. USC, whatever its defensive lapses in the Riley era, has a legitimate opportunity to make this uncomfortable. Still, Ohio State has a significant defensive advantage overall, allowing just 13 points per game and has an important edge countering the Trojans' ground game that can reduce that offense to one dimension. USC will have opportunities, but Ohio State's defensive consistency ultimately proves to be the edge in the second half. The Big Lead prediction: Ohio State 30, USC 23

Pete Fiutak Wed, October 28, 2026 at 5:02 PM UTC · 4 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads It's Ohio State. It's among the most super of superpowers. It's one of those programs with no excuses. It gets just about any player it wants, its realistic expectations are national title or bust, and it's one of the few programs that can lose its starting quarterback and still reasonably be considered the No. 1 team in the country. But now it has to go at least the next several weeks without star quarterback Julian Sayin, who injured his shoulder in the win over Indiana a few weeks ago. There's a quarterback battle to see who steps into the role as the team travels to Los Angeles to face a desperate USC team in a whole lot of trouble. The Trojans are 6-2, but they just got stuffed by Wisconsin in a punishing 24-7 loss, and with a brutal schedule to close, the Lincoln Riley hot seat is flaming. On the plus side, win, and the team is still deep in the College Football Playoff hunt. Ohio State vs USC: Quick Hits It doesn't get any easier for USC with a trip to Indiana next after a week off, and then Maryland, and it all closes at UCLA. Ohio State finishes with three of its last four games in Columbus, hosting Oregon next week. The road game is at Nebraska. This is the first time these two have met since a 24-7 Ohio State win in the 2017 Cotton Bowl. USC has won seven or the last eight in the series goning back to the 1974 Rose Bowl. How To Watch Ohio State vs USC Date: Saturday, October 31, 2026 Game Time: 7:30 PM ET TV: NBC Location: Los Angeles Memorial Coliseum, Los Angeles, CA – Week 9 Schedule, Game Previews – CFN Top 25 | Bowl Projections – Predicting the First CFP Top 25 – CFN Week 9 Expert Picks Why Ohio State Will Win USC just isn't that great. It has a wonderful 6-2 record, quarterback Jayden Maiava is terrific, and there's still pop and explosion to worry about, but there are flaws. It beat Washington and Penn State, but lost at home to a struggling Oregon, and couldn't get anything going against the Badgers. Ohio State isn't the Ohio State of previous seasons, but it's still good enough to beat anyone else this year. To win, the Buckeyes have to screw up, but USC doesn't take the ball away with just six turnovers forced on the season, and there's little running game to worry about. USC ran well on Rutgers and Louisiana, and that's about it. Slow down the midrange USC passing game, slow down USC. Why USC Will Win If Ohio State didn't exactly go turn-it-loose full-throttle with Julian Sayin under center, what will it do with Luke Fahey and/or Tavien St. Clair? Both are talented prospects, and no matter who is under center, there's still Jeremiah Smith and a loaded receiving corps to throw to, but this is where the offense has to rely on the running game, and it might not be able to do it. The Buckeyes are averaging a pedestrian four yards per carry, and were stuffed by Indiana two weeks ago, gaining just 37 yards. Fahey missed both of his throws against Indiana, and St. Clair has only seen the lightest of mop-up work so far. Ohio State vs USC Prediction, Betting Lines Which team has another gear? Can USC's run defense ball out, and can Jayden Maiava play like the best quarterback on the field? Or will the Ohio State defense step up and keep the big pass plays to a minimum? Yes, Indiana came within a few inches from beating Ohio State, but Josh Hoover only hit 50% of his passes, and only Arch Manning has been able to complete more than 56% against the Buckeyes. Maiava will have a nice day, but the Trojans will stall a bit too often. It won't be pretty, but the Buckeyes will take advantage of a few good field position chances to survive and advance in a relatively low-scoring game. away.headline: Report: Ohio State makes logical QB decision ahead of USC showdown
away.blurb: While Fahey and St. Clair battled it out this season, the writing was on the wall. Despite St. Clair being a coveted prospect in the 2025 recruiting class, it was Fahey who has been No. 2 on the depth chart. St. Clair was a five-star prospect out of Bellefontaine (OH) and has seen action in two games this season off the bench. He completed 5-of-7 passes for 52 yards and one touchdown, along with one interception. Ohio State starting quarterback Julian Sayin exited the Indiana game two weeks ago after sustaining an injury. Head coach Ryan Day said the Buckeyes are preparing to be without Sayin for the remainder of the season, which puts a major question mark on Ohio State. When Sayin left the game, it was freshman Luke Fahey who came in for Sayin. But during the Buckeyes’ bye week, Day wasn’t tipping his hand as to who Ohio State would start against USC . However, according to a report from CBS Sports’ Matt Zenitz , Ohio State is planning on starting Fahey over redshirt freshman Tavien St. Clair. This season, Fahey has completed 9-of-13 passes for 203 yards, two touchdowns, and two interceptions. MORE: 4 bold college football predictions for Week 9: Ohio State has major QB issues Fahey will make his first collegiate start against the Trojans on Saturday. While the timing isn’t ideal, what is ideal is having Jeremiah Smith at your disposal. The Buckeyes not only have arguably the best player in college football, but Ohio State also has a great receiving corps. The three-star freshman from Mission Viejo (CA) is also going up against the No. 14 passing defense in the Big Ten. The Trojans allow 216 yards per game through the air and Fahey has a chance to impress in his first start. Ohio State has struggled to run the football this season and Fahey will likely need to stretch the defense to get Ohio State rolling. The game will kick off Saturday at 7:30 p.m. ET on NBC.

Skip to main content SI.COM TRANSFER PORTAL Bears In The Pros Baylor stares down UCF on Friday night as they try to avoid a third straight loss. The Bears torched UCF in Waco last November 30-3 and will try to rinse and repeat on the road. UCF is undefeated on their home turf and is coming off a dramatic victory over No. 2 BYU, making them 1.5-point favorites over the Bears. Here are three predictions for Joe Klanderman's debut in Baylor's Week 9 matchup: It will still feel like Aranda's team The Bears have parted ways with Dave Aranda after seven years, and Joe Klanderman has stepped into the interim head coach role. Klanderman had just five days to get this team into shape before UCF. While his methods and leadership may be strong, it is surely hard to turn a football team on its head in less than a week. With offensive coordinator Jake Spavital still in charge of the offensive playcalling, I doubt Baylor is going to look dramatically different than they did against Kansas. Doesn't mean the Bears can't win, but it will take more time to see major, positive change in the intangibles. picks.blurb: 2026 Week 9 Space Game Preview: Baylor Bears @ UCF Knights - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football College Football Playoff NFL injury tracker Belichick-Hudson breakup Brewers' championship parade Chet Holmgren injury Fantasy Start 'Em, Sit 'Em 2026 Week 9 Space Game Preview: Baylor Bears @ UCF Knights ORLANDO, FLORIDA - OCTOBER 24: Keyone Jenkins #12 of the UCF Knights reacts after a touchdown in the first half of the game between the UCF Knights and BYU Cougars at Acrisure Bounce House on October 24, 2026 in Orlando, Florida. (Photo by Dustin Markland/Getty Images) | Getty Images Steve Helwick Thu, October 29, 2026 at 9:12 PM UTC · 8 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Time and date: Friday, October 30 at 7:30 p.m. ET Network: ESPN Location: Acrisure Bounce House — Orlando, FL Spread: Baylor (-1.5) Over/under: 48.5 All-time series: Baylor leads, 2-1 Last meeting: Baylor 30, UCF 3 — November 1, 2025 Current streak: Baylor, 2 (2023-25) Setting the scene Baylor and UCF have only met three times, but there is no shortage of iconic moments between these programs. UCF entered the 2013 Fiesta Bowl as a 13.5-point underdog to Big 12 champion Baylor. However, Blake Bortles led the Knights to an electrifying 52-42 victory on New Year's Day, sealing the program's first-ever AP Top 10 finish. Ten years later, UCF held a 35-7 lead in the late third quarter over Baylor, but the Bears rallied with 29 unanswered, surviving a wild fourth down conversion and a 59-yard field goal attempt to hold onto a 36-35 win. Perhaps another memorable finish awaits as the programs meet in Orlando for the 10th annual Space Game. UCF continues one of college football's most recognizable modern traditions, rebranding to the "Citronauts" for a night and donning space-themed alternate uniforms as a nod to the university's aeronautical roots. The Citronauts are one of the better teams in college football history, owning an 8-1 record in Space Games and outscoring opponents by an aggregate result of 432-189: 2017 – UCF 63, East Carolina 21 2018 – UCF 52, Temple 40 2019 – UCF 44, Houston 29 2020 – UCF 51, Tulane 34 2021 – UCF 24, Memphis 7 2022 – UCF 70, Temple 13 2023 – UCF 45, Oklahoma State 3 2024 – UCF 56, Arizona 12 2025 – Houston 30, UCF 27 However, Houston defeated UCF in last year's Space Game, spoiling the Citronauts' perfect record. UCF, coming off its first top-5 victory in program history, aims to recapture its galactic momentum as Baylor strolls into the Bounce House. Baylor Bears outlook WACO, TEXAS - SEPTEMBER 19: Defensive Coordinator Joe Klanderman of the Baylor Bears yells from the sideline during the second quarter during the game against the Louisiana Tech Bulldogs on September 19, 2026 at the McLane Stadium in Waco, Texas. (Photo by Hanna Kotlarek/Baylor Athletics/University Images via Getty Images) Baylor (4-3, 2-2 Big 12) fired head coach Dave Aranda in the middle of his seventh season in Waco. Aranda's tenure was quite volatile, featuring highs of a 12-2 finish and Big 12 championship in 2021, but lows including a 3-9 record in 2023. The Bears lacked consistency under Aranda, improving or declining by at least three wins in every year from 2019 through 2025. Baylor moves forward with interim Joe Klanderman, who also retains his defensive coordinator duties. In year one on campus, Klanderman has done a stellar job reforming Baylor's defense. He implemented a 3-3-5 base scheme and vastly improved the unit, allowing them to skyrocket from 122nd to 19th in scoring defense and 122nd to 22nd in run defense. The Bears let up just 16.1 points per game, and last Saturday's 25-24 loss to Kansas was the first time they surrendered more than 17 points all season. The defense showed promise even in losing efforts, falling 17-16 to Auburn and 17-6 to TCU. Baylor is the best in the Big 12 at getting to the quarterback and its 3.9 sacks per game rank third nationally. There isn't one dominant pass rusher, rather, it's a concerted effort. Edge rusher Garrick Ponder leads the charge with 4.0 sacks while safeties Daniel Cobbs and Bo Onu are tied for second with 3.0 apiece. With great pressure comes great chaos, and Baylor is producing takeaways at a high rate. The team ranks 15th nationally with 13 takeaways, and strong safety Micah Gifford has been omnipresent with three interceptions and two fumble recoveries. While the passing defense has more interceptions than touchdowns allowed, and forces opponents to a 59.8 completion rate, Baylor still allows 236 passing yards per game, which ranks 103rd nationally. Teams regularly hit explosives on the Bears, which have given up 13 passes of 30 yards or greater through seven games. Last season, Baylor excelled offensively and struggled on defense. This year, the opposite is true. Outside of the 55-19 rout at Arizona State, the Bears have not been able to consistently generate points. They scored 24 or fewer points in four of seven games, and all three losses were attribute to a lack of scoring. Still, quarterback DJ Lagway has moved the ball well for the nation's 24th-ranked passing offense. The veteran starter averages 270 passing yards per game, delivering nine touchdowns and four interceptions. Efficiency has been an issue through the air though, and Baylor checks in at 124th in the FBS with a 56.4 completion rate. Wide receiver Gavin Freeman operates as the main target. His 58 receptions are the second-most in the country and his 678 receiving yards rank second in the Big 12. Louis Brown and Jayden McGowan are among Lagway's other frequented options. Baylor hasn't been as lethal on the ground, still awaiting its first 90-yard rusher of the season. The Bears were held to 54 rushing yards against TCU and 122 against Kansas — a significant reason Baylor enters Orlando on a two-game losing streak. UCF Knights outlook ORLANDO, FLORIDA - OCTOBER 24: Keyone Jenkins #12 of the UCF Knights celebrates a touchdown in the first half of the game between the UCF Knights and BYU Cougars at Acrisure Bounce House on October 24, 2026 in Orlando, Florida. (Photo by Dustin Markland/Getty Images) | Getty Images UCF (4-3, 2-2 Big 12) is coming off a win for the ages. Although the Knights won multiple New Year's Six bowls and secured an NCAA-recognized national championship in 2017, last Saturday's double overtime triumph over No. 2 BYU was the program's first-ever top-5 victory in history. It was the long-awaited signature win of Scott Frost's second tenure in Orlando and restored energy into a fanbase, which will certainly show up in droves for the annual Space Game. There were moments throughout the BYU game where it appeared UCF missed a golden opportunity for an upset. However, the Knights stayed the course and won just their second October game in their last 13 tries. One of the heroes last week was quarterback Keyone Jenkins, who threw for 293 yards and three touchdowns, while rushing for an additional score in the 39-31 win. After witnessing several strong performances by the FIU transfer, Frost named Jenkins the starting quarterback moving forward, even though original starter Alonza Barnett III has recovered from a Week 2 hamstring injury. UCF has received stronger support from the passing attack in recent weeks, which has been efficient. The Knights have thrown 13 touchdowns against four interceptions, while completing 66.5 percent of attempts this year. It hasn't been the most explosive unit, completing just seven passes spanning 30 yards and two spanning 40, but Jenkins has allowed the Knights to piece together methodical possessions. The run game has been the hallmark of UCF's offense all season. Running back Duke Watson is eighth in the Big 12 in rushing and averages 6.8 yards per carry. Landen Chambers has also stepped up from the backfield lately, scoring two touchdowns in last week's win over BYU. But the true emerging star in UCF's offense is true freshman wide receiver Tyren Hornes. After being underutilized in September, Hornes has become one of the top options for the Knights, producing 137 yards on six receptions last Saturday. He now ranks second on the team in receiving yards behind Josh Derry, who leads all Knight receivers in catches (34), yards (358), and touchdowns (3). Although the last two weeks were more offensive oriented games, UCF has been best on the defensive side this year. The Knights allow 23.0 points per game, allow just 3.2 yards per rushing attempt, and hold opponents to a completion rate of 58.9 percent. However, UCF must play the Space Game without arguably its best defensive player. Strong safety Demari Henderson suffered an injury in overtime against BYU, and the team will miss his production, which includes 35 tackles, two interceptions, and five pass breakups. The Knights still have several veteran faces in the secondary including cornerbacks Antione Jackson and Jayden Bellamy, who both have one interception and one forced fumble on the season. Thanks to these defensive backs, UCF is a plus-5 in the turnover battle this season. Can UCF avoid a letdown after an emotional win? Signature wins haven't been easy to follow up in college football this season. Auburn beat Georgia and then lost by 21 to LSU at home. BYU took down Notre Dame and then dropped an overtime thriller to UCF a week later. Ole Miss' triumph over LSU was followed by a thrashing at the hands of Florida. And so on. Baylor also had an eventful week, as the Bears move on from head coach Dave Aranda and now must respond with an interim head coach in a hostile Orlando environment. The Bears' defense has been consistently sound this year, and UCF may struggle to come close to its Space Game average of 48 points per game. The defenses control this matchup, and the Bears prevent a successful launch with a game-winning field goal in the final minute. Prediction: Baylor 24, UCF 21

picks.blurb: Predicting Final Score of Baylor Bears vs. UCF Knights in Week 9 Without Dave Aranda - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football College Football Playoff NFL injury tracker Belichick-Hudson breakup Brewers' championship parade Chet Holmgren injury Fantasy Start 'Em, Sit 'Em IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Trent Knoop, Blake Hollingsworth, Brad Teague & Tyler Gillum Fri, October 30, 2026 at 1:00 PM UTC · 5 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads It's been a disastrous two weeks for the Baylor Bears. After dominating Arizona State and looking like the Bears could be a real threat, Baylor suffered back-to-back losses to TCU and Kansas, dropping the Bears to 4-3 on the season . The loss to Kansas also ended the Dave Aranda era in Waco. In his seventh season, Aranda was fired and Joe Klanderman will lead the Bears for the remainder of the season as the interim head coach . Klanderman looks to reignite the Baylor Bears and have a strong finish to the season. Baylor will look to get back into the win column on Friday night when the Bears take on UCF . Here's how the staff of Baylor on SI sees the game going. IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Baylor's defense has been great this season and Klanderman has re-established the Bears' defense. But you have to wonder if there will be any setbacks from Dave Aranda not being on the sidelines any longer and Klanderman taking on the head coach role, while calling the defense. UCF has a good offense and Keyone Jenkins has been legit . The Knights just beat BYU and a hangover is certainly possible, but it's not like Baylor has been playing great football. What worries me is the Bears' offensive line. DJ Lagway has been asked to do everything for this offense, and the offensive line can't block for the run game. If Baylor can't run the ball again, it's going to be tough sledding. I look for the home team to make one too many plays. Final score: UCF 27, Baylor 24 Baylor comes off a tough loss to Kansas and has a shorter week facing off against a UCF team that just beat the number 2 ranked team in the country. Should be mostly a passing game given the defenses in this matchup. Baylor has struggled to get the run game going and UCF has had one of the best run defenses in the country right now. Expect a high air-raid offense from both sides, and multiple touchdowns. Baylor will be in their first game without head coach Aranda after getting let go Sunday. My guess is that they will pull one together and slightly outscore this team coming off a big win. Final score: Baylor 30, UCF 23 After the past two weeks saw Baylor lose to TCU and Kansas, fire Dave Aranda, name Joe Klanderman interim head coach, and have a shortened week of preparation for their Friday night contest against UCF, the Bears are up against the wall in terms of their season. They've officially hit the big red "panic" button on the season and fired Aranda in hopes of seemingly not losing the entire fan base. However, the competition still remains, and even with Aranda no longer with the team, the offense is still the same squad that has been struggling to produce since returning to play after the bye week. Baylor's defense is going to cause havoc for UCF's QB Keyone Jenkins and probably even record another 4+ SK 7+ TFL game. Potentially even forcing Jenkins into throwing an interception or two, the outcome of this game won't be the fault of the Bears' defense. There's only so much one side of the ball can do, after all. If the Bears O-line remains unable to successfully push back the opposing D-line, it's going to again lead to three-and-outs or otherwise quickly ended drives. Not to mention that an unsuccessful O-line will inevitably force DJ Lagway into uncomfortable throws and rushed decisions against UCF's team currently in the top 20 in the nation with a +5 turnover margin. Penalties have been a big problem for the Bears this season, especially last week, totaling a dozen for 116 yards. Averaging 74 yards a game in penalties is rough and only hurts the Bears overall. However, I don't expect that trend to end any time soon, maybe not for over 100 yards, but Baylor is going to give up a lot of yards that they didn't have to again this week. I would love nothing more than to watch the offense and defense come out and click on all cylinders, but this has been a not-so-normal week. Fully expecting the Bears to be competitive, I don't however expect them to be able to overcome their recent struggles offensively. Final score: UCF 20, Baylor 17 Blake Hollingsworth Hopefully I'm wrong, but I just don't see Baylor coming out on top in interim head coach Joe Klanderman's debut. UCF is unbeaten at home and coming off a double-overtime upset of previously undefeated No. 2 BYU. DJ Lagway should have a few chances to connect on deep passes against a UCF defense allowing nearly 240 passing yards per game. However, the Knights lead the Big 12 with 12 forced turnovers, including seven interceptions, which could be a problem for a Baylor offense averaging only 17.3 points in its four Power Four matchups outside its blowout win over Arizona State. Baylor's defense will keep the game competitive per usual, but the Bears' struggles with penalties, red-zone efficiency and offensive consistency are difficult to overlook. With UCF carrying momentum into Friday's matchup, I'm picking the Knights to hand Baylor its third consecutive loss. It will also mark the first game without Dave Aranda on the sideline . In his seventh season in Waco, Aranda was fired after the Bears suffered another heartbreaking loss. away.headline: 5 Questionable Decisions That Defined Dave Aranda's Baylor Tenure
away.blurb: 5 Questionable Decisions That Defined Dave Aranda's Baylor Tenure Skip to main content SI.COM Here are five of the most questionable decisions of Aranda's Baylor tenure. Aranda had reason to overhaul Baylor's defensive staff following the 2022 season, but his choice of replacement proved questionable. Continuing to direct the defense while overseeing the entire program raised questions about whether Aranda had taken on too much. Although his defensive expertise was never in doubt, the arrangement potentially limited the attention he could devote to recruiting, roster construction and other head coaching duties. Dave Aranda's tenure at Baylor peaked in 2021, when the Bears won a program-record 12 games, captured the Big 12 championship and claimed a Sugar Bowl victory. Nearly five years later, he was fired following Saturday's 25-24 loss at Kansas, finishing his six-plus seasons in Waco with a 40-40 record. Baylor's decline can't be traced to a single mistake, but several of Aranda's decisions played a role in the program's inability to sustain its success. Some made sense at the time but ultimately backfired, while others were mistakes he later acknowledged. 1. Being Slow to Embrace the Transfer Portal Nov 22, 2025; Tucson, Arizona, USA; Detailed view of the jersey of Baylor Bears quarterback Sawyer Robertson (13) against the Arizona Wildcats at Casino Del Sol Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Mark J. Rebilas-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Aranda's emphasis on player development helped establish the culture behind Baylor's 2021 championship, but that same philosophy arguably kept the Bears from adapting quickly enough to college football's changing roster landscape. Aranda's emphasis on player development helped establish the culture behind Baylor's 2021 championship, but that same philosophy arguably kept the Bears from adapting quickly enough to college football's changing roster landscape. Baylor added only 10 scholarship transfers during Aranda's first three seasons before bringing in 12 during the 2023 cycle. While other programs increasingly used the portal to address immediate needs, the Bears remained more reliant on developing players already on their roster. Aranda later acknowledged struggling with bringing in transfers when doing so could mean passing over players he had recruited and developed. That reluctance became particularly costly following the 2021 season, when Baylor lost several important contributors, including Jalen Pitre, JT Woods, Terrel Bernard and Abram Smith. Replacing that experience and production was never going to be easy, but the transfer portal offered opportunities to address weaknesses before they became bigger problems. Instead, Baylor struggled to maintain the depth and physicality that had helped it win the conference championship. home.headline: UCF's Scott Frost Shares Injury Updates Ahead of Space Game
home.blurb: Coach Scott Frost said running back Taevion Swint will be back quickly, and linebacker Lewis Carter could be a game-time decision this week . He added that if the senior isn't available against the Baylor Bears, he'll likely be a game-time decision next Saturday against the Kansas Jayhawks . Carter has missed every conference game this season. He went into the medical tent for a knee injury at the end of Week 3's win over the Georgia State Panthers and was ruled out early for the next game. UCF's Scott Frost Shares Injury Updates Ahead of Space Game - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF Brewers' championship parade Fantasy Start 'Em, Sit 'Em UCF's Scott Frost Shares Injury Updates Ahead of Space Game (Mike Watters/Imagn Images) Demetrius Montero Tue, October 27, 2026 at 9:00 PM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads The UCF Knights made program history in upsetting the then-No. 2 BYU Cougars , and a few key players are on the cusp of returning for Friday's Space Game. Swint's injury occurred in practice, and Frost said he started limping after a "nothing play." The redshirt freshman missed his first game of the season , leaving room for Landen Chambers to step up in his absence. UCF has relied on the speedster to make plays in the run game and on special teams. Swint's rushed for 162 yards and two touchdowns on 32 carries, and returned seven kickoffs for 209 yards. He scored his first touchdown in the season opener against the Bethune-Cookman Wildcats, and the second in the Big 12 home opener against the TCU Horned Frogs . The Knights have missed their defensive quarterback, especially in highly contested losses against the then-No. 20 Houston Cougars and then-No. 18 Oklahoma State Cowboys . The senior had a career season last year after transferring from Oklahoma . Carter led the team with 92 tackles and set career highs in tackles for loss, sacks, and fumbles. He became a star at UCF. While at Oklahoma, he was a reserve linebacker and special teams player. Wisconsin transfer Tackett Curtis, the team's leading tackler, has stepped up in Carter's absence. Curtis has 42 tackles (18 solo, 24 assisted), one sack, one fumble recovery, one pass deflection and two interceptions. The Knights are getting healthy at the right time. They aim to build on an upset win and collect two more wins to break a two-year bowl drought. Friday's game against Baylor is one of the more interesting weekday matchups . The program fired coach David Aranda, and Joe Klanderman is the interim coach. UCF's eight-game Space Game winning streak ended in heartbreaking fashion as Houston caught the game-winning interception against former Knights quarterback Davi Belfort.
